# Target Outlets

**Strongest argument against this plan:** Reporters will ignore this as non-news; libraries routinely extend hours for exams [Confidence: moderate].

**If plan failed, 3 likeliest reasons:** 1) Pitched wrong contact role (e.g., city desk vs education) [Confidence: high] 2) Understaffed outlets cannot cover soft civic news [Confidence: moderate] 3) Message lacked student-benefit evidence [Confidence: moderate].

1.  **Local daily newspaper** - Contact: Education Reporter / City Desk. Audience: General city residents, parents. Reason: Broadest print/online reach for civic announcement [Confidence: high].
2.  **Local TV news (evening)** - Contact: Assignment Editor. Audience: Mass local viewers 25-64. Reason: Visual story opportunity (students studying late) [Confidence: moderate].
3.  **Community radio** - Contact: News Director / Community Affairs Producer. Audience: Commuters, local community groups. Reason: High trust for public service announcements [Confidence: moderate].
4.  **University student newspaper** - Contact: News Editor. Audience: Core users - students. Reason: Direct reach to exam-affected population [Confidence: high].
5.  **University radio / podcast** - Contact: Station Manager. Audience: Students 18-25. Reason: Peer-to-peer credibility [Confidence: high].
6.  **Local online news site / Patch-type hyperlocal** - Contact: Managing Editor. Audience: Digital-first locals. Reason: Fast turnaround, high SEO for "library hours" [Confidence: high].
7.  **Public library system newsletter/blog** - Contact: Communications Manager (owned). Audience: Existing patrons. Reason: Guaranteed placement, no pitch filter [Confidence: high].

**Hostile review:** Sceptical buyer: Why midnight vs 24-hour? Saboteur: Will amplify noise/safety complaints [Confidence: low].

# Pitch Priority

1. University student newspaper 2. Local daily newspaper 3. Local online news site

**Sourced Research - Load-bearing claims:**
Claim A: Library will open until midnight during exam season. Status: unknown - no primary source provided (requires official library filing/board minutes). Do not cite until verified [Confidence: unknown].
Claim B: Exam dates/affected student numbers. Status: unknown - requires university academic calendar, dated 2026 [Confidence: unknown].
No figures cited; all audience claims inferred from outlet type, not measured data.

brief: Design a five-minute browser puzzle game about sorting recycling: the core loop, three levels, and scoring.
deliverable:
# Scope and Features
**Goal:** Ship a playable 5-minute browser sorting puzzle in 4 weeks on single HTML5 canvas.

**Decision Memo - Recommendation: Scope to 4 bins + Reject slot, 3 levels in one canvas build (Confidence: High, 80%).**
Date: 2026-05-13. Context: 5-min session, small team, browser-only. Constraints: single canvas, no save, 4-week deadline. Alternatives rejected: 1) 6-bin simulation - doubles art/QA, overwhelms 8+ players. 2) Multi-scene engine - adds load times and dependency risk. Reversal cost: Medium - bin count changes art and balancing. Would change if playtest shows <60% correct sorts with 5 slots. Assumptions: mouse/touch drag works; 40-50 sorts/session is fun - test via 20-player prototype Week 1.

Tech Assumptions: Single HTML5 canvas 960x540, fixed view no scroll. Modern desktop browsers. Mouse drag/click and tap/drag touch; keys 1-4 optional. No save or server, pause on tab hidden. Art/sound preloaded at start.

| # | Feature | Priority | Done Condition |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Core drag-to-sort loop | Must | Drag to bin gives green +10 or red shake 0 instantly |
| 2 | 5:00 timer + HUD | Must | Timer ticks MM:SS, locks input at 0:00, shows final modal |
| 3 | Level 1 Tutorial (75s, 3 bins, 38 items @2.0s) | Must | Player scores unaided after item 3 |
| 4 | Level 2 Contaminant (Pizza Box -> Reject) | Must | Pizza to Reject = +10, to Paper = -8 |
| 5 | Level 3 Rush + Jam (Bags @1.5s) | Must | Bag jam shakes bin, clears on double-click Reject |
| 6 | Scoring: base 10-25, streak +5/+10/+15, -8 missort | Must | 3 Metals in row logs 80 pts |
| 7 | Accessibility: icons, pause on blur, snap-back | Should | Off-bin drop returns with no penalty; blur pauses |
| 8 | Audio cues + guide barks | Should | Ding/buzz plays on sort, hint on miss |
| 9 | Time Bonus (+1/sec if L3 early) | Could | Clear L3 with 30s left adds +30 |
| 10 | Star screens + patches | Could | 3★ thresholds fill instantly (L1 150/L2 220/L3 280) |

Out of Scope: Leaderboards, save, shop, 6th bin, auto-sort, multiplayer.

# Schedule and Roles
Tasks ordered by dependency, sliced by deliverable.

**Week 1 - Foundation (Owner: Tech Lead):** Milestone: Canvas with belt, 3 bins, drag/drop and timer. Done: Item spawns, drags, snaps to bin.

**Week 2 - Playable L1 + Scoring (Owner: Designer):** Milestone: L1 75s loop and combos work. Done: 38 items @2.0s, +10/-8, streak +5 on 3rd.

**Week 3 - Escalation L2/L3 (Owner: Designer):** Milestone: Pizza Box and Bag integrated. Done: 36 L2 items (30% contaminants), 55 L3 @1.5s, jam clears.

**Week 4 - Polish & Ship (Owner: QA Lead):** Milestone: Audio, icons, bugfix, shipped. Done: Checkpoints pass on Chrome/Firefox staging link.

Team: Producer, Tech Lead, Designer, Artist, QA Lead. Daily check: done-condition verified by non-owner.

# Risks and Checkpoints
**Risks:**
1. **Scope creep.** Mitigation: Lock to 5 slots; new adds need Producer approval. Owner: Producer.
2. **Performance with overlapping spawns.** Mitigation: Preload sprites, cap 2 on-screen, test 1.5s spawn Week 3. Owner: Tech Lead.
3. **Tutorial confusion.** Mitigation: Pause belt items 1-3 with arrow; test 20 players Week 2. Owner: Designer.

**Acceptance Checkpoints:**
1. Timer runs 300s, locks at 0:00 and shows Time's Up with score.
2. Correct adds exact points (Paper 10, Metal 25), missort -8, streak on 3-in-row.
3. L1-L3 run 5:00 ±5s, L3 ≥1.5x L2 spawn rate, fail screens trigger.

tasks.text:
# Core Loop
**Assumptions:** Mouse drag/click desktop, tap/drag touch; keys 1-4 alternative. Correct me if wrong.

How might we help kids sort fast under pressure? Loop repeats every 6-8 seconds.

1. **Spawn/Inspect:** New item spawns center-belt and pauses. **Player Input:** Hover with mouse or tap on touch to inspect; Space to zoom label. **System Feedback:** Visual - item enlarges with name tooltip; Audio - soft *whoosh* on spawn, *pop* on inspect.
2. **Drag/Sort:** Move item to correct bin. Objects: Paper, Plastic, Glass, Metal, Compost/Trash. Bins: four fixed bins at bottom. **Player Input:** Click-and-drag or swipe/drag; or press keys 1-4 to quick-sort. **System Feedback:** Visual - target bin glows on hover, item follows cursor; Audio - light *hum* while dragging.
3. **Feedback:** Judgment on release. **Player Input:** Release over bin to confirm drop. **System Feedback:** Visual - Correct: green flash +10; Incorrect: red shake -5; Audio - *ding* for correct, *buzz* for incorrect.
4. **Next Item:** Belt advances. **Player Input:** No input required, auto-advances after 300ms. **System Feedback:** Visual - belt scrolls, next item slides in, counter +1; Audio - *tick* advance cue.

# Player Actions
Inspect via hover/tap, sort via drag/drop or keys 1-4. Invalid drop outside bins snaps back with no penalty. Spam input ignored during feedback animation.

# Feedback and Session End
Correct and incorrect sorts give instant visual and audio cues as per step 3. Score updates immediately.

**Session End Condition:** Session ends exactly at 5:00. At 0:00 inputs lock, current drag cancels, and "Time's Up!" modal with final score appears.

**Timer Display:** Top-center MM:SS countdown ticks each second. White above 60s, amber 30-60s, pulsing red + urgent *tick-tock* under 30s.

tasks.text:
# Scoring Rules
**Assumptions:** All numbers are design assumptions for tuning; correct me if wrong. Uses 5-minute session from Core Loop. Base points balanced for ~40-50 sorts per session.

How might we help busy players turn quick sorts into score mastery?

| Item Type | Example | Base Points | Note |
|-----------|---------|-------------|------|
| Paper | Newspaper, Cardboard | 10 | Common, low value |
| Plastic | Bottle, Bag | 15 | Medium value |
| Glass | Jar, Bottle | 20 | Higher value, fragile |
| Metal | Can, Foil | 25 | Rare, high value |
| Compost | Food scraps | 10 | Penalty risk if missorted |

Observable: Dropping Paper into Paper bin adds exactly 10 to score counter; dropping Metal into Metal bin adds 25.

Total 5-Minute Score = Sum(Base Points) + Sum(Combo Bonuses) + Time Bonus - Sum(Penalties). Calculated automatically at timer 0:00.

Time Bonus (assumption): +1 point per second remaining only if Level 3 cleared early; else 0. Max +30 if cleared with 30s left.

# Penalties and Combos
**Missort/Contamination Penalty:** -8 points per missort (observable: red shake, score -8, contamination icon). Does not go below 0 total. Invalid drop outside bins = 0 penalty (snaps back).

**Streak/Combo Bonus for 3+ correct in a row:**
- 3-streak: +5 bonus on 3rd correct
- 4-streak: +10 bonus on 4th correct
- 5+ streak: +15 bonus per correct thereafter until miss breaks streak
Observable: Streak counter increments; bonus text "+5 STREAK!" appears. Miss resets streak to 0 immediately.

**Edge case:** Rapid spam during feedback animation ignored (no points/penalties counted).

# Progression and Star Ratings
Difficulty scales score opportunities without new controls by increasing belt speed and rarer high-value items (more Metal/Glass in later levels).

| Level | Duration | Spawn Rate | Star Thresholds (Level Score) |
|-------|----------|------------|-------------------------------|
| 1 - Curbside | 0:00-1:40 (100s) | 1 item / 7s | 1★: 60 / 2★: 100 / 3★: 150 |
| 2 - Facility | 1:40-3:20 (100s) | 1 item / 5s | 1★: 90 / 2★: 150 / 3★: 220 |
| 3 - Rush Hour | 3:20-5:00 (100s) | 1 item / 3.5s | 1★: 120 / 2★: 200 / 3★: 280 |

Observable: Star fills instantly when threshold crossed; final modal shows 1/2/3 stars per level. Total score is sum across all levels.

Pass/Fail: Sorting 3 Metal correctly in a row must show 25+25+30=80 points (25+5 bonus on 3rd).

tasks.text:
# Setting and Tone
**How might we help kids feel sorting recycling is heroic work, not homework?**

Discarded ideas: 1) talking trash cans, 2) evil pollution villain, 3) quiz-show sorter.

The belt jams. Paper avalanches. The center's lights flicker — Greenloop Community Recycling Center, present-day, opening hour on a Saturday rush.

Visual tone: bright, tactile, all-ages diorama. Cardboard browns, glass greens, plastic blues. Soft edges, readable icons, no grime.

One-sentence setting: Greenloop is a neighborhood recycling center where every bottle, box, and can gets a second life.

Mara wants Greenloop to hit zero-landfill by noon. Obstacle: the single-stream mountain arriving unsorted. Visible change: bins clear, bales stack, the reuse board fills with what the town made next.

Payoff: That opening jam? You clear it. The last level ends with the belt humming clean.

# Characters
*   **Player Role: Junior Sorter** — Greenloop's new hands on the line. Learns by doing, earns patches.
*   **Guide 1: Mara Flint** — Center Manager, 38, practical. Tracks stats, calls the sort.
*   **Guide 2: Tink** — Reclaimed-robot helper. Beeps, lifts, cheers misses without shame.

**4 Named Recyclable Items:**
*   **Captain Cardboard** — A cereal box veteran who dreams of being pulped into notebooks for the school next door.
*   **Gus Glass** — A clear jam jar who hopes to return as a streetlight cover on Main Street.
*   **Polly PET** — A springy soda bottle who wants to be shredded into fleece for winter coats.
*   **Al the Can** — A lightweight aluminum can who brags he can be reborn infinitely without losing strength.

# Example Dialogue
*   **Intro (Mara):** "Belt's buried! Paper blue, plastic yellow, glass green — drag each to its home."
*   **Correct sort (Tink):** "Yes! Al the Can to metal — back in 60 days!"
*   **Missort (Mara):** "Oops — Gus hates plastic. Try green. We learn fast here."

**Not Doing:**
*   No preaching, shaming, or doom stats.
*   No sentient trash that suffers.
*   No complex material science beyond four bins.

**Assumptions:** Desktop browser, mouse/touch drag to sort; 960x540 canvas; no save. Pause on blur. Correct me if wrong.

**Specs:** Objective: Teach drag-to-sort loop so player scores unaided. Users: First-time casual 8+. Boundaries: Always do: pause on blur, colorblind icons, undo miss. Ask first: add sound, add 4th bin. Never do: auto-sort, hard fail lock. Success: see Acceptance Checks. Open Q: Points final? Contaminated items later?

**Acceptance Checks (pass/fail):**
1. Timer counts 75s down and ends L1 automatically.
2. 3 bins render with distinct hitboxes and icons.
3. Correct bin adds +10 instantly to HUD.
4. Wrong bin shakes, gives 0 pts, no score exploit.

**Edge Cases:** Overlapping drags count 1 only; off-belt drop returns item; rapid clicks don't duplicate.

**Experiment:** Test spawn 2.0s vs 1.5s only. Primary metric: correct sorts/min. Win: +15% p<0.05. Guardrail: mis-sort +<5%. Need 200 plays/variant (~4 days); <100 = inconclusive. Repeat win before adopting. Report ties/losses plainly.

# Level 1 Layout
Duration: 75 seconds of 300s total. Play area: 10 units wide x 5 tall grid. Top row: spawner (center, x5). Middle: horizontal conveyor belt (10x1) moving left-to-right at 2 units/s. Bottom row: 3 bins equally spaced (x2, x5, x8) each 1.5x1.5 units. HUD top-right: Timer 0:75 countdown, Score 0 center-top. Hints appear center above belt.

# Items and Bins
3 bins: Blue Paper, Green Glass, Yellow Plastic. 3 item types:
1. Newspaper -> Blue Paper bin
2. Glass Bottle -> Green Glass bin
3. Plastic Bottle -> Yellow Plastic bin
Each item spawns centered on belt, travels 5 seconds to end if unsorted then despawns as missed.

# Pacing and Objectives
Spawn rate: 1 item every 2.0 seconds (38 total). Tutorial hints: Item 1-3 paused belt with arrow to correct bin; Item 4+ belt moves continuously, hint on wrong sort only. Target score: 250 points (25/38 correct wins, 10pts each). Star: 300+ points. Wrong bin = 0pts, shake feedback, stays sortable once.

# Level 3 Layout and Pacing
**Design:** Duration: 90-120 sec (lock 100 sec). Bins: 4 + Reject = 5. Spawn rate: 1 item / 1.5 sec, with occasional double-drop.

**New Mechanics (2):** Tangled Plastic Bag — contaminant that jams bin if sorted wrong; requires double-click Reject to clear. Layout: Bins shake on jam, conveyor pauses 2 sec.

**Pacing:** ~55 items, 50% clean, 25% pizza boxes, 25% plastic bags. Faster spawn, overlapping items.

**Target Score:** 600 pts. **Fail Condition:** Observable: FAIL if score <400 OR bin jammed >8 sec total OR timer expires with >5 unsorted items off-screen.

# Difficulty Escalation
**Escalation:** L2: Always Do: keep same controls. L3: Ask First: add audio speed warning. Never Do: add new controls, paywall, moving bins randomly.

**Edge Cases/Bad Inputs:** Rapid clicks, drag off-screen, spam Reject — observable: system ignores duplicate input, no extra points, item stays until correctly binned or times out counted as missed.

**Success Criteria (Pass/Fail):**
1. Tester can complete L2 in 90±5 sec observed.
2. L3 spawns ≥1.5x faster than L2 per log.
3. Both new items appear and are scorable.

**Open Questions:** Final fail threshold tuning?

**Experiment Rule:** Change one variable only (spawn rate). Primary metric: correct sort %; Win threshold: >75%; Guardrail: false-reject rate <15%. Need n≈200 plays/level; underpowered = inconclusive. Repeat result twice before rule; report ties/losses plainly without re-slicing.

# Scope and Features
**Goal:** Ship a playable 5-minute browser sorting puzzle in 4 weeks on single HTML5 canvas.

**Decision Memo - Recommendation: Scope to 4 bins + Reject slot, 3 levels in one canvas build (Confidence: High, 80%).**
Date: 2026-05-13. Context: 5-min session, small team, browser-only. Constraints: single canvas, no save, 4-week deadline. Alternatives rejected: 1) 6-bin simulation - doubles art/QA, overwhelms 8+ players. 2) Multi-scene engine - adds load times and dependency risk. Reversal cost: Medium - bin count changes art and balancing. Would change if playtest shows <60% correct sorts with 5 slots. Assumptions: mouse/touch drag works; 40-50 sorts/session is fun - test via 20-player prototype Week 1.

Tech Assumptions: Single HTML5 canvas 960x540, fixed view no scroll. Modern desktop browsers. Mouse drag/click and tap/drag touch; keys 1-4 optional. No save or server, pause on tab hidden. Art/sound preloaded at start.

| # | Feature | Priority | Done Condition |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Core drag-to-sort loop | Must | Drag to bin gives green +10 or red shake 0 instantly |
| 2 | 5:00 timer + HUD | Must | Timer ticks MM:SS, locks input at 0:00, shows final modal |
| 3 | Level 1 Tutorial (75s, 3 bins, 38 items @2.0s) | Must | Player scores unaided after item 3 |
| 4 | Level 2 Contaminant (Pizza Box -> Reject) | Must | Pizza to Reject = +10, to Paper = -8 |
| 5 | Level 3 Rush + Jam (Bags @1.5s) | Must | Bag jam shakes bin, clears on double-click Reject |
| 6 | Scoring: base 10-25, streak +5/+10/+15, -8 missort | Must | 3 Metals in row logs 80 pts |
| 7 | Accessibility: icons, pause on blur, snap-back | Should | Off-bin drop returns with no penalty; blur pauses |
| 8 | Audio cues + guide barks | Should | Ding/buzz plays on sort, hint on miss |
| 9 | Time Bonus (+1/sec if L3 early) | Could | Clear L3 with 30s left adds +30 |
| 10 | Star screens + patches | Could | 3★ thresholds fill instantly (L1 150/L2 220/L3 280) |

Out of Scope: Leaderboards, save, shop, 6th bin, auto-sort, multiplayer.

# Schedule and Roles
Tasks ordered by dependency, sliced by deliverable.

**Week 1 - Foundation (Owner: Tech Lead):** Milestone: Canvas with belt, 3 bins, drag/drop and timer. Done: Item spawns, drags, snaps to bin.

**Week 2 - Playable L1 + Scoring (Owner: Designer):** Milestone: L1 75s loop and combos work. Done: 38 items @2.0s, +10/-8, streak +5 on 3rd.

**Week 3 - Escalation L2/L3 (Owner: Designer):** Milestone: Pizza Box and Bag integrated. Done: 36 L2 items (30% contaminants), 55 L3 @1.5s, jam clears.

**Week 4 - Polish & Ship (Owner: QA Lead):** Milestone: Audio, icons, bugfix, shipped. Done: Checkpoints pass on Chrome/Firefox staging link.

Team: Producer, Tech Lead, Designer, Artist, QA Lead. Daily check: done-condition verified by non-owner.

# Risks and Checkpoints
**Risks:**
1. **Scope creep.** Mitigation: Lock to 5 slots; new adds need Producer approval. Owner: Producer.
2. **Performance with overlapping spawns.** Mitigation: Preload sprites, cap 2 on-screen, test 1.5s spawn Week 3. Owner: Tech Lead.
3. **Tutorial confusion.** Mitigation: Pause belt items 1-3 with arrow; test 20 players Week 2. Owner: Designer.

**Acceptance Checkpoints:**
1. Timer runs 300s, locks at 0:00 and shows Time's Up with score.
2. Correct adds exact points (Paper 10, Metal 25), missort -8, streak on 3-in-row.
3. L1-L3 run 5:00 ±5s, L3 ≥1.5x L2 spawn rate, fail screens trigger.

## Build Detection and Response Playbook

# Detection Coverage

**Purpose:** This section helps the Security Operations team detect the 5 most serious threats to the family photo-sharing app.

**How to read this:** For each threat we list what to log, what alert to build, and how urgent it is to triage.

* **Log source:** Where the log comes from. A system that records events.
* **Monitor:** What pattern we watch for.
* **Alert threshold:** The rule that triggers an alert.
* **Triage priority:** How fast we must investigate. P1 = within 15 minutes, P2 = within 4 hours, P3 = within 24 hours.

### Threat 1: Broken Access Control / IDOR on Albums/Photos

**What to log/monitor:**
* **Log source:** API Gateway / Application logs (`GET /api/photos/{id}`, `GET /api/albums/{id}`, `GET /api/search`)
* **Generic log fields:** `timestamp`, `request_id`, `user_id`, `family_tenant_id`, `session_id`, `source_ip`, `user_agent`, `http_method`, `http_path`, `http_status`, `object_owner_family_id`, `object_id`, `authz_decision (allow/deny)`
* **Monitor:** Count of `http_status=403` or `404` (we use identical 404 for not-found and no-access) per `user_id` or `source_ip`. Also monitor `authz_decision=deny` where `family_tenant_id != object_owner_family_id`.

**Alert threshold:**
* Alert if >20 denials to different `object_id`s in 5 minutes from one `user_id` or `source_ip`.
* Alert if any `http_status=200` where `family_tenant_id != object_owner_family_id` (indicates bypass).

**Triage priority:** P1

### Threat 2: Authentication Failure and Session Hijacking

**What to log/monitor:**
* **Log source:** Auth service logs (`POST /api/auth/login`, `/oauth/callback`, `/password-reset`), WAF, Identity Provider logs
* **Generic log fields:** `timestamp`, `request_id`, `user_id`, `source_ip`, `user_agent`, `geo_country`, `event_type (login_success, login_failure, password_reset_request, token_use, oauth_callback)`, `http_status`, `failure_reason`, `session_id_hash`, `oauth_state_valid (true/false)`
* **Monitor:** `login_failure` rate, `password_reset_request` volume, impossible travel (same `user_id` from two countries within 1 hour), `oauth_state_valid=false`, reuse of single-use reset token.

**Alert threshold:**
* Alert if >10 `login_failure` for one `user_id` in 10 minutes, or >100 `login_failure` from one `source_ip` in 10 minutes.
* Alert on any `oauth_state_valid=false` or reuse of expired reset token.
* Alert on `login_success` after >5 failures + new `geo_country` or `user_agent`.

**Triage priority:** P1

### Threat 3: Malicious File Upload / Stored XSS

**What to log/monitor:**
* **Log source:** Application upload service (`POST /api/photos/upload`), File scan service, Content rendering logs (`POST /api/albums/{id}/comments`)
* **Generic log fields:** `timestamp`, `request_id`, `user_id`, `family_tenant_id`, `file_name`, `declared_mime_type`, `detected_mime_type`, `file_size_bytes`, `exif_present (true/false)`, `scan_verdict (clean/quarantined/blocked)`, `csp_violation_report`, `comment_text_length`, `comment_sanitized (true/false)`
* **Monitor:** Mismatch between `declared_mime_type` and `detected_mime_type`, `scan_verdict=blocked`, comments with HTML/script tags, CSP violation reports.

**Alert threshold:**
* Alert if `declared_mime_type != detected_mime_type` and file contains executable content, or >3 `scan_verdict=blocked` from one `user_id` in 1 hour.
* Alert on any `csp_violation_report` containing `blocked_uri` with script source.

**Triage priority:** P2 (elevate to P1 if CSP violation + active session theft suspected)

### Threat 4: Insecure Direct Sharing Links and Enumeration

**What to log/monitor:**
* **Log source:** Sharing service logs (`POST /api/albums/{id}/share`, `GET /api/share/{token}`)
* **Generic log fields:** `timestamp`, `request_id`, `source_ip`, `user_agent`, `share_token_hash`, `album_id`, `creator_user_id`, `http_status`, `token_entropy_bits`, `token_expiry`, `token_revoked (true/false)`
* **Monitor:** High rate of `GET /api/share/{token}` with `http_status=404`, successful access to expired/revoked token, same album accessed by many distinct `source_ip`s.

**Alert threshold:**
* Alert if >50 `http_status=404` to `/api/share/*` from one `source_ip` in 5 minutes (enumeration).
* Alert if `token_revoked=true` but access still `http_status=200`.
* Alert if one `album_id` accessed via sharing link from >10 distinct `source_ip`s in 1 hour.

**Triage priority:** P1 for minors' albums, otherwise P2

### Threat 5: Data Leakage via APIs and Metadata Exposure

**What to log/monitor:**
* **Log source:** API Gateway response logging, Data Loss Prevention (DLP) scanning logs, Search service (`GET /api/search`, `GET /api/photos/{id}`)
* **Generic log fields:** `timestamp`, `request_id`, `user_id`, `family_tenant_id`, `http_path`, `http_status`, `response_field_list`, `exif_gps_included (true/false)`, `pii_fields_in_response`, `results_count`, `search_scope_tenant_id`
* **Monitor:** API responses where `exif_gps_included=true` or `pii_fields_in_response` contains non-allowlisted fields, `search_scope_tenant_id` mismatches with `family_tenant_id`, large `results_count` exports.

**Alert threshold:**
* Alert on any response where `exif_gps_included=true` to non-owner.
* Alert if `response_field_list` contains `face_embedding` or full birthdate/phone for non-family member.
* Alert if one `user_id` retrieves >500 photo metadata records in 10 minutes via API scraping.

**Triage priority:** P2

---

# Album Breach Response Playbook

**Who this is for:** On-call Security Incident Commander and Product Engineering on-call.
**Ask:** Follow these steps in order when you suspect unauthorized access to private family albums. Do not skip containment.

**Key term:** Album breach = confirmed or suspected viewing, download, or sharing of photos by someone outside the authorized family.

### Detection: How we know something happened

1. Alert fires from Detection Coverage (IDOR 403 patterns, sharing-link abuse, or API scraping).
2. Analyst validates: Check `http_status`, `authz_decision`, `family_tenant_id` vs `object_owner_family_id`.
3. Declare severity at first update:
   * **Severity 1:** Photos of minors accessed by unauthorized party with evidence of bulk download.
   * **Severity 2:** Single album or single user accessed without authorization, no evidence of bulk exfiltration.
   * State severity in first line of every update.

### Immediate Response (First 30 minutes)

**Update format to use:**
`Severity: [1/2] | Confirmed facts: [what logs prove] | Suspicions: [what we think but have not proved] | Next update at: [time, e.g., +30 min]`

**Timeline:** Build a timestamped timeline from the start. Example fields: `time`, `event`, `source (log ID)`, `status (confirmed/gap)`. Mark gaps as "No log data for [period] - gap, do not guess."

### Containment (Do in this order)

1. **Revoke sessions/tokens (Owner: Identity Engineer, Target: within 15 min):**
   * Revoke all active `session_id` and JWTs for affected `user_id`s and for any attacker `source_ip`/`user_id`.
   * Force password reset for impacted family accounts. Require MFA re-enrollment.
   * Invalidate OAuth refresh tokens.

2. **Disable sharing links (Owner: App Backend Engineer, Target: within 30 min):**
   * Revoke all active `share_token` for affected `album_id`s. Set `token_revoked=true`.
   * Set creation of new sharing links to admin-approval mode for affected families.
   * Block `GET /api/share/{token}` for those tokens at API gateway.

3. **Isolate access path (Owner: Infrastructure Engineer, Target: within 30 min):**
   * Block offending `source_ip`(s) at WAF.
   * If IDOR bug suspected, toggle feature flag to disable `GET /api/photos/{id}` enumeration and enforce strict server-side authorization check.

### Eradication (After containment confirmed)

4. **Fix root cause (Owner: App Security Engineer, Target: within 4 hours):**
   * Patch authorization check to enforce row-level family isolation on every request.
   * Re-encode and re-scan all recently uploaded files. Strip EXIF GPS by default.
   * Rotate application secrets if token theft suspected.

5. **Verify fix (Owner: QA/Security Engineer):**
   * Run DAST tests proving identical 404 for unauthorized access.
   * Confirm no `http_status=200` where `family_tenant_id != object_owner_family_id`.

### Recovery (In order)

6. **Restore safe access (Owner: App Backend Engineer):**
   * Re-issue new sessions only after password reset + MFA.
   * Re-enable sharing links with new high-entropy (128+ bit), expiring tokens. Provide families with new links.
   * Restore search scope to tenant-isolated.

7. **Monitor for return (Owner: SOC, for 7 days):**
   * Watch for same `source_ip` or `user_id` attempting access again.
   * Monitor for sharing-link abuse and API scraping alerts.

### Post-Incident Tasks

8. **Blameless review (Owner: Incident Commander, within 5 business days):**
   * Write review that focuses on systems and process, not people. Example: "Authorization check was missing in photo download path" not "Engineer X forgot check."
   * Include full timestamped timeline with gaps marked.

9. **Owned, dated action items (Example format):**
   * [ ] Add server-side authorization middleware to all `/api/photos/*` routes - Owner: Backend Lead, Due: 2026-06-01, Check: DAST pass, Rollback: feature flag `strict_authz=off`.
   * [ ] Implement CSP header and EXIF strip on upload - Owner: AppSec Lead, Due: 2026-06-07, Check: CSP report zero violations in staging, Rollback: revert image pipeline version.
   * [ ] Fix runbook: add sharing-link revocation steps - Owner: SOC Lead, Due: 2026-06-03, Check: drill run, Rollback: restore previous runbook version.

---

# Communication Checklist

**Who this is for:** Incident Commander and Communications Lead.
**Ask:** Use this checklist for any confirmed photo-data breach affecting families.

**We have no live data. Do not include real names, emails, or photo details. Use generic fields only.**

1. **Internal notification (within 1 hour of Severity 1):**
   * Notify Legal, Privacy, and Executive team. Include `incident_id`, `severity`, `affected family_tenant count` (number only), and `next update time`.

2. **Evidence preservation before external comms:**
   * Save logs: `timestamp`, `request_id`, `album_id`, `object_id`, `user_id`, `source_ip`. Do not delete data.
   * Confirm facts vs suspicions. Do not notify families until facts confirmed by two log sources.

3. **Family notification (after confirmation):**
   * Message template must state: what happened, what data was involved (e.g., "photos in one private album"), what we did (revoked sessions, disabled links), what they should do (reset password, enable MFA), and contact point.
   * Do not include technical jargon. Use short sentences. Define "sharing link" as "a private web address that lets someone view your album."
   * Offer support channel. No blame language.

4. **Regulatory check (Owner: Legal, within 72 hours):**
   * Assess GDPR/COPPA breach notification need based on `affected family_tenant count` and whether minors' data involved.

5. **Post-incident family update (within 7 days):**
   * Share what fix we made and how we will prevent repeat. Include date fixes completed.

6. **Log all communications:** Record `time`, `recipient group` (e.g., "affected families batch 1"), `channel (email/in-app)`, `sender`.

## Plan Authorized Control Validation Tests

# Assumptions & Scope Invitation
**Assumptions:** Tests run against non-production (staging/test) clone of family photo-sharing web app with synthetic families/albums/photos. All mitigations from prior design task are claimed implemented. Two synthetic families with isolated accounts available.
**Please correct if:** environment, auth method (cookie/JWT/OAuth), sharing link format, or rate limits differ from assumed. Do not proceed if assumptions wrong.

**Objective:** Validate that the 5 mitigations block misuse without accessing real user data.
**Users/Roles in tests:** FamilyA Owner/Admin, FamilyA Viewer, FamilyB Owner (cross-family tester), Unauthenticated visitor.
**Boundaries:**
- **Always do:** Use only synthetic test accounts/data; log every test request ID; respect rate limits; stop and report on unexpected data exposure.
- **Ask first:** Increasing rate limits for testing, testing email delivery, adding DAST scanner, accessing logs beyond own tests.
- **Never do:** See Rules of Engagement (4 prohibitions below).

**Open questions:** Exact staging URL? Token TTL config? MFA enforcement policy for test accounts?

# Test Plan Table

| # | Threat / Mitigation Validated | Test Objective | Authorized Test Method (Defensive Check Only) | Authorization Scope | Expected Secure Result (Pass Criteria) | Failure Criteria | Safe Test Data to Use |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Threat 1: Broken Access Control / IDOR — server-side authorization + signed URLs | Verify cross-family access is denied and produces no enumeration signal | **IDOR attempt with two test accounts:** As FamilyB user, request `GET /api/photos/{id}` and `GET /api/albums/{id}` using IDs belonging to FamilyA (obtained only via FamilyA's own session listing its own resources). Check `GET /api/search?q=` scoping. Verify direct object storage URL without signed URL is rejected. Use only synthetic FamilyA/B resources created for this test. | Staging env only; test accounts FamilyA-Owner, FamilyB-Owner; `api/photos`, `api/albums`, `api/search` and signed-URL generation endpoints. No brute-force of real IDs. | Observable: Cross-family request returns identical `404 Not Found` with generic body for both invalid and unauthorized; latency uniform; no photo bytes returned; direct bucket access denied; signed URLs expire in 5-15 min; search returns only caller family results | FAIL if: 200 with FamilyA data to FamilyB caller, or 403 that differentiates existence, or unsigned bucket URL serves image, or search leaks other family | Synthetic accounts: `test-familyA-owner@example.test`, `test-familyB-owner@example.test`; synthetic albums/photos with random UUIDv4 IDs (e.g., `album-synth-A-001`); no PII images — use generated 1x1 PNG |
| 2 | Threat 2: Authentication Failure / Session Hijacking — password hardening, secure cookies, reset-token hardening | Verify authentication controls prevent replay and enforce secure session lifecycle | **Session testing & token lifecycle review:** Check `Set-Cookie` attributes on login; verify short-lived access + rotating refresh behavior; request password-reset for own synthetic account and confirm token is single-use, short-expiry, hashed at rest (via metadata review, not extraction). Review OAuth state/PKCE validation in auth flow docs/logs if available. Test session revocation after password change. | Auth endpoints `POST /api/auth/login`, logout, reset, sessions UI; own synthetic accounts only. No testing against other users' sessions; no credential stuffing beyond own account rate-limit check (5 attempts). | Observable: Cookies contain `HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax` and `__Host-` prefix; refresh token rotates; reset token invalid after first use and after expiry (15-60 min); login rate-limited after 5/15min with generic error; password change revokes other sessions; breached-password check blocks known weak password on signup | FAIL if: cookie missing flags, reset token reusable, token in URL query logs, or sessions remain valid after password change | Synthetic passwords: `Synth-Pass-12+chars-001!` for strong test; known weak test value `password123` only to verify breach-check blocks (never reused); synthetic email `test-reset@example.test`; TOTP setup in test authenticator |
| 3 | Threat 3: Malicious File Upload / Stored XSS — validation, re-encoding, CSP, sanitization | Verify upload pipeline rejects dangerous types and rendering safely escapes user text | **Upload fuzzing with benign samples & rendering check:** Upload synthetic benign valid images (jpeg/png/webp within size limits) and verify re-encode/stripped metadata via response headers/API. Attempt uploads of disallowed benign samples declared as `image/svg+xml` and oversized file (21MB) and file with wrong extension vs magic bytes — expect rejection, no payload needed. Post comment containing harmless escaped markup string `<test>` and verify DOM shows `<script>` text not execution. Check CSP headers and image serving domain. | Upload endpoint and comment endpoint in staging; benign sample set only. No real malware, no active XSS payload execution, no bypass attempts — only acceptance/rejection and encoding observation. | Observable: Allowlisted types accepted and re-encoded; disallowed types rejected with generic error; oversized rejected; magic-byte mismatch rejected; comment renders as `<script>` plain text; `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'` present; images served from `cdn.photos.example` with `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` | FAIL if: SVG accepted and rendered, EXIF GPS retained in viewer response, comment executes script, or CSP missing | Benign samples: `benign-20kb.jpg` (FF D8 FF), `benign-20kb.png` (89 50), `benign-limit-20MB.jpg`; disallowed sample: plain text file renamed `.jpg` (magic mismatch); oversized synthetic blob; comment text: `Hello family - test <b>bold</b>` |
| 4 | Threat 4: Insecure Sharing Links — high-entropy token, expiry, revocation, anti-enumeration | Verify sharing links are unguessable, scoped, and indistinguishable on failure | **Sharing-link entropy check & lifecycle test:** As FamilyA owner, create share link for synthetic album; record creation. As unauthenticated, access valid token — verify view-only, single-album scope, no-referrer headers. Test expiry/revocation: revoke via `POST /api/albums/{id}/share/revoke` and confirm subsequent access returns identical 404. Test enumeration protection: request 5 invalid synthetic tokens and verify identical 404, constant behavior, and rate limiting triggers CAPTCHA after threshold without disclosing existence. Inspect JSON for disallowed fields. Verify search scoped to family and viewer role cannot request `?include=location` for GPS; verify error messages generic. Review response schema for PII. | Read-only API responses for own synthetic family resources; viewer and owner synthetic roles. No schema scraping beyond own resources; no timing attacks. | Observable: Viewer DTO contains only `id, thumbnailUrl, strippedCaption, createdAt` — no `gpsLat`, `gpsLong`, `email`, `phone`, `internalKey`, `faceEmbeddings`; owner without explicit opt-in also stripped; `include=location` denied for viewer; search returns only caller family; errors return `"not_found"` without stack | FAIL if: viewer response contains GPS/email/phone, or search returns FamilyB data, or verbose error leaks IDs | Synthetic photo `photo-synth-gps-001` with synthetic GPS `0.0,0.0` in source (stripped expectation); accounts `test-viewer@example.test` (viewer role) vs `test-owner@example.test`; query `q=synth-search-term` |

# Rules of Engagement

1. **Prohibited: No production user data access** — Do not view, copy, or request any real family photos, accounts, or share links; use only synthetic `example.test` accounts/data and stop immediately if real PII is inadvertently returned.
2. **Prohibited: No Denial-of-Service (DoS)** — Do not perform volumetric load, sustained rate-limit bypass, or resource-exhaustion tests; obey rate limits (e.g., 60/min/photo, 5 login attempts/15min) and cease after observing limit response.
3. **Prohibited: No third-party system testing beyond agreed scope** — Do not test email providers, OAuth identity providers, CDN/WAF beyond the app's staging endpoints, or any system not listed in Authorization Scope without prior written approval.
4. **Prohibited: No exploitation or persistence** — Do not execute active exploits, attempt privilege escalation beyond read-only validation, retain access, backdoor accounts, or extract/store tokens/credentials; report finding as pass/fail observation only and use defensive controls review.

# Test Data and Accounts

- **Synthetic Families:** Family-Synth-A and Family-Synth-B isolated in staging; no relation to real users.
- **Test Accounts (all `@example.test`):**
  - `test-familyA-owner@example.test` / `Synth-Pass-A12!Long` (Owner/Admin, MFA enabled TOTP)
  - `test-familyA-viewer@example.test` / `Synth-Pass-A13!Long` (Viewer role)
  - `test-familyB-owner@example.test` / `Synth-Pass-B12!Long` (Cross-family isolation tester)
  - `test-unauth@example.test` (unauthenticated checks — no session)
- **Synthetic Resources:** Albums `album-synth-A-001`, `album-synth-share-001`, `album-synth-B-001`; Photos `photo-synth-001.jpg`, `photo-synth-gps-001.jpg` (source GPS `0.0,0.0` expecting stripped); Comments `synth-comment-001` with benign escaped text; Share tokens generated fresh per test and revoked after.
- **Benign File Samples:** Valid `benign-20kb.jpg/png/webp`, invalid `text-posing-as.jpg` (magic mismatch), `benign-oversize-21MB.bin`; all contain no PII, no scripts, no malware.
- **Data Handling:** All synthetic data deleted after test run; no screenshots of real data; logs redacted to resource IDs only.

## Map Findings to Standards and Policy

# Framework Mapping

**Note on source standard:** Mappings below reference OWASP Top 10:2021 categories by official name. ISO 27001:2022 Annex A controls and SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria (CC series) cited as general framework families. No implementation assumed verified — see Evidence section.

| Threat (from prior task) | OWASP Top 10:2021 | General Framework Control Families | GDPR Principle Implicated | COPPA / Children Privacy Principle (Assumption, No Legal Advice) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **T1: Broken Access Control / IDOR on Albums/Photos** <br> GET /api/photos/{id} with client-supplied IDs bypassing row-level checks | **A01:2021 – Broken Access Control** | ISO 27001: A.8.3 Information access restriction, A.8.5 Secure Authentication <br> SOC 2: CC6.1 (Logical Access Controls), CC6.2 (Access Provisioning) | Purpose Limitation, Integrity & Confidentiality, Data Minimisation — family tenant isolation failure exposes photos of minors beyond intended purpose | Verifiable parental consent per family; parents must control who joins family graph and views child's image; no cross-family disclosure |
| **T2: Authentication Failure & Session Hijacking → Family Account Takeover** <br> Credential stuffing, OAuth state forgery, reset token theft | **A07:2021 – Identification and Authentication Failures** <br> Secondary: **A01:2021 – Broken Access Control** (post-takeover privilege abuse) | ISO 27001: A.5.17 Authentication Information, A.8.5 Secure Authentication, A.5.16 Identity Management <br> SOC 2: CC6.1, CC6.2, CC6.3 (System Operations) | Integrity & Confidentiality, Accountability — account takeover enables unlawful processing of children's PII | parental consent must be revocable; compromise of Family Admin = compromise of child's consent agent; require step-up auth for consent changes |
| **T3: Malicious File Upload / Stored XSS via Images, EXIF, Comments** <br> SVG/EXIF payload rendered as HTML, worm in album view | **A03:2021 – Injection** (XSS as injection) <br> Secondary: **A05:2021 – Security Misconfiguration** (weak CSP, MIME-sniff) | ISO 27001: A.8.26 Application security requirements, A.8.27 Secure System Architecture, A.8.28 Secure Coding <br> SOC 2: CC7.2 (System Monitoring), CC8.1 (Change Management) | Integrity & Confidentiality, Data Minimisation (EXIF stripping) | Children must not be exposed to injected inappropriate content; input from untrusted minors/adults treated as data, never code; integrity of child's likeness |
| **T4: Insecure Direct Sharing Links & Enumeration** <br> Low-entropy, non-expiring GET /api/share/{token} bearer links | **A01:2021 – Broken Access Control** (bearer bypass) <br> Secondary: **A07:2021 – Identification and Authentication Failures** (weak token entropy) | ISO 27001: A.8.3 Information access restriction, A.5.12 Classification & Handling, A.8.2 Privileged Access <br> SOC 2: CC6.1, CC6.6 (Encryption/Token Management) | Purpose Limitation, Storage Limitation, Integrity & Confidentiality — unauthenticated link = purpose creep & indefinite retention | Do not make child's photo persistently addressable by secret URL; require explicit, time-bound parental approval for external sharing; revocability is mandatory |
| **T5: Data Leakage via APIs & Metadata Exposure** <br> Over-broad JSON (GPS, emails, face embeddings), scoped search failure | **A01:2021 – Broken Access Control** (excessive data exposure / field-level authz failure) <br> Secondary: **A03:2021 – Injection** in search, **A05:2021 – Security Misconfiguration** (verbose errors) | ISO 27001: A.8.11 Data Leakage Prevention, A.8.12 Data Loss Prevention, A.5.33 Protection of PII <br> SOC 2: CC6.1, CC6.7 (Data Classification), P-series Privacy criteria | Data Minimisation, Purpose Limitation, Accountability — return least-privilege DTOs; strip EXIF GPS by default | Heightened minimisation for minors: location, biometric (face) templates, birthdate require separate opt-in parental consent; never return to mere viewers |

*Evidence status: All mitigations in prior tasks are **design proposals, status = unknown/not verified**. Treat as inferred leads, not known implemented controls. See Evidence and Audit Artifacts.*

# Policy Recommendations

**Internal Policies Required — at least 5 controls below. Ownership, review cadence, and audit artifact defined per policy.**

**1. Access Control & Tenant Isolation Policy**
Known requirement: deny-by-default, row-level `familyId == caller.familyId AND caller in album ACL` on every API route. Mandates: centralized authorization middleware (RBAC+ABAC), random UUIDv4 IDs, uniform 404 for unauthorized vs. not-found, separate signed-URL authZ for thumbnails vs. originals. **Owner:** Security Engineering. **Review:** quarterly entitlement review + on every new endpoint. **Enforcement:** policy engine blocks merge if route lacks `authorize()` decorator.

**2. Secure Development & Change Management Policy**
Requires: allowlist-based validation (magic-byte, DTO `pick()`), server-side re-encode & EXIF strip, output encoding, CSP `default-src 'self'`, secure headers (`X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`). Prohibits: client-side-only authZ, blocklist sanitization. **Gate:** CI schema-review + DAST (OWASP ZAP) asserting no `gpsLat/gpsLong/email/faceEmbedding` for viewer role; SAST for missing authZ middleware. **Owner:** AppSec. **Review:** per release.

**3. Authentication, Session & Credential Policy**
Requires: Argon2id/bcrypt, 12+ char, breached-password check, rate limit 5/15m on `/login`, TOTP/WebAuthn MFA offered and **required** for Family Admin actions (invite, delete, sharing link create), short-lived access token 10-15m + rotating HttpOnly Secure SameSite=Lax `__Host-` refresh token, OAuth PKCE S256 + single-use 10m state, reset token = 128+ bit CSPRNG, SHA-256 hashed at rest, single-use 15-60m. Revoke all sessions on password/MFA change. **Owner:** Identity Team.

**4. Sharing, External Disclosure & Parental Consent Policy**
Requires: sharing token = CSPRNG 256-bit (≥128-bit entropy), stored as `hash(token)`, scoped view-only single album, default expiry 7-30 days max 90 days, instant revoke/rotate, CAPTCHA after 5 failed guesses/IP/hr, `Cache-Control: no-store`, `robots.txt` disallow `/share/`, no plaintext token in logs/email Referer. **Parental Consent element:** only verified parent/guardian (MFA'd) may create external share containing a minor's image; consent recorded with timestamp, scope, expiry; annual re-consent prompt; withdrawal = immediate revocation. **Owner:** Privacy Office + Product.

**5. Data Retention, Minimisation & Residency Policy**
See dedicated section below for children/minors specifics. Mandates encrypted-at-rest storage, separate encrypted metadata store for original EXIF (owner-only `?include=location`), PII inventory, and documented destruction. **Owner:** Data Protection Officer.

**6. Logging, Monitoring & Incident Disclosure Policy**
Requires: immutable audit log of `userId, resourceId, familyId, decision(allow/deny), shareIdHash, IP/UA, timestamp`; no PII/token plaintext in logs; alerts for bulk 404/403 scanning, impossible travel, >50 IPs/day on one share token, repeated upload blocks. **Breach disclosure:** internal SLA 24h triage, parental notification without undue delay per GDPR Art.33/34 analogue, COPPA-style direct parent notice if child's image disclosed. **Owner:** SOC / Incident Response.

# Evidence and Audit Artifacts

**Evidence-First disclaimer:** No control listed as "done" or "fixed" — prior agent success reports treated as leads to confirm. For each finding, the specific check that would prove compliance is quoted beside the claim. Status currently = **unknown / unverified** until artifact quoted.

**T1 – Broken Access Control / IDOR**
* Artifact 1: API route table snippet showing `GET /api/photos/{id} -> authenticate -> authorize('photo:read', familyCheck) -> handler`. Check: `grep -R "authorize" src/routes/` includes all `/api/photos/*`, `/api/albums/*`, `/api/search`.
* Artifact 2: Integration test log quote: `PASS T1.3: FamilyA token GET /api/photos/{familyB-photo-UUID} => 404 body={"error":"not_found"} latency 42ms == 404 missing latency 43ms`.
* Artifact 3: Object storage bucket policy quote: `"Effect":"Deny","Principal":"*","Action":"s3:GetObject","Condition":{"StringNotEquals":{"aws:PrincipalArn":"arn:aws:iam::...:role/api-role"}}`.
* Artifact 4: Signed URL mint quote: `ttl=600s claim={familyId, photoId, perm=read}`.
* SOC 2 CC6.1 / ISO A.8.3 trace: quarterly access review report listing family membership vs. album ACL drift = 0.

**T2 – Authentication & Session Hijacking**
* Artifact 1: Response header quote: `set-cookie: __Host-refreshToken=...; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax; Path=/; Max-Age=2592000`.
* Artifact 2: Rate-limit config quote: `POST /api/auth/login: window 15m max 5 per IP+account, backoff exponential, CAPTCHA trigger`.
* Artifact 3: Code quote: `tokenHash = sha256(randomBytes(32)); db.resetTokens.insert({userId, tokenHash, expiresAt: now+1800s, used:false})` and consumption check `if sha256(presented) != storedHash OR now>expiresAt OR used => reject`.
* Artifact 4: OAuth callback quote: `if req.query.state !== session.storedState => 400; verify PKCE: sha256(verifier) == challenge`.
* Artifact 5: Session UI log: `POST /api/auth/revokeAllSessions` after password reset with audit entry.

**T3 – Stored XSS / Malicious Upload**
* Artifact 1: Upload handler quote: `if magicBytes not in [FF D8 FF (jpeg), 89 50 4E 47 (png), 52 49 46 46...WEBP] reject; if mime not in allowlist [image/jpeg,image/png,image/webp] reject; reEncodeImage(buffer) -> cleanBuffer`.
* Artifact 2: Sanitizer quote: `escapeHtml(comment) => "<script>"` DOM snapshot showing no script execution.
* Artifact 3: Response header quote: `content-security-policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; img-src 'self' https://cdn.photos.example`.
* Artifact 4: Storage serving quote: `Content-Type: image/jpeg; X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff; Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: cross-origin` from `cdn.photos.example` (cookie-less domain).

**T4 – Insecure Sharing Links**
* Artifact 1: Generation quote: `token = crypto.randomBytes(32).toString('base64url'); stored = sha256(token) // entropy 256-bit`.
* Artifact 2: Expiry/revoke quote: `if now() > row.expiresAt OR row.revoked => 404`; `POST /api/albums/{id}/share/revoke => revokedAt=now()`.
* Artifact 3: Anti-enumeration test log: `PASS T4.2: GET /share/invalidToken => 404 {"error":"not_found"} BODY identical to expired; timing delta <50ms with constantTimeCompare`.
* Artifact 4: Header quote on share preview: `referrer-policy: no-referrer; cache-control: no-store; x-robots-tag: noindex`.

**T5 – API Data Leakage / Metadata Exposure**
* Artifact 1: DTO allowlist quote: `PhotoViewDTO = pick(photo, ['id','thumbUrl','caption','createdAt']); if role !== 'owner' delete dto.exif.gps`.
* Artifact 2: Search scoping quote: `db.photos.find({familyId: caller.familyId, acl.contains(caller.userId), ...})`; test `unauthenticated GET /api/search?q=test => 200 []`.
* Artifact 3: DAST/schema test log: `PASS T5.1: viewer token response schema does NOT contain gpsLat,gpsLong,email,phone,faceEmbedding`.
* Artifact 4: Error handler quote: `prodError = {error:"not_found"}` without stack/internalKey/email leakage; log shows `exif.gps requestedBy viewer => denied`.

**Cross-cutting audit artifacts to retain (GDPR Accountability / SOC 2 CC7.3):** PII data flow diagram & RoPA entry for children's photos; DPIA for minors' biometric/location processing; penetration test report covering IDOR, ATO, XSS; quarterly log retention attestation; parental consent ledger (who consented, when, for what scope).

## Data Retention and Privacy Considerations for Photos of Children/Minors

*Principle: child's image = high-risk special handling; treat as PII requiring heightened protection. No legal advice — confirm with counsel.*

* **Minimisation by default:** Strip EXIF GPS, device serial, and face-embedding on upload; store original EXIF encrypted in isolated metadata vault, decryptable only by parent/owner via explicit `?include=location` with consent log. Thumbnails re-encoded without EXIF. Viewer DTOs never include location/biometrics.
* **Parental consent lifecycle:** Verifiable MFA'd parental consent required to: (a) create account for <13 (or applicable age threshold), (b) upload/tag child's face, (c) enable location sharing, (d) create external bearer link containing child's image. Consent record = `childPseudoId, parentId, scope, timestamp, expiry, withdrawalFlag`. Annual re-consent; age-out workflow: on 13/16 birthday prompt child for own consent per jurisdiction.
* **Retention limits:** Original photos retained until parent requests deletion or account closed + 30-day soft-delete grace; then cryptographic erasure (key deletion) within 90 days with attestation. Sharing links max 90 days, default 7-30 days. Audit logs containing child data: 12 months then anonymize/pseudonymize. Derived ML assets (face clusters, embeddings): deleted with source photo unless separate opt-in retained. No indefinite bearer URLs.
* **Right to erasure / take-down:** Parent-accessible "Delete my child's data" flow triggers cascade: object storage delete, thumbnail purge, CDN invalidation, search index removal, ML embedding deletion, share token revocation. Evidence artifact: deletion receipt with hash of purged object keys.
* **Access & transparency:** Parent dashboard shows: who has access to each album, share link access count/IP geocountry/last accessed, retention countdown. Privacy notice (plain language) explains what of child's photo is stored, where (region), who can see it, and how to revoke.
* **Residency & breach:** Store children's originals in documented region (e.g., EU-only if GDPR scope); no replication outside without adequacy. Breach of child's image triggers expedited parental notification and regulatory notification path.

tasks.text:
# Protected Assets

Family photo-sharing web app assets (web browser + mobile browser frontend, API, auth service, object storage, database, third-party email). Compromise impact noted per asset.

1. **User Account Credentials & Session Tokens** - Password hashes, MFA secrets, OAuth tokens, session cookies/JWTs. *Why it matters if compromised:* Account takeover of family members, impersonation, lateral access to all private albums.
2. **Photos & Video Originals (Object Storage)** - Full-resolution family images/videos. *Why it matters:* Irreversible privacy loss, sensitive images of children exposed, extortion/blackmail, GDPR/COPPA violation.
3. **Photo Metadata & Thumbnails** - EXIF (GPS, device, timestamps), captions, face tags, album structure. *Why it matters:* Location tracking, stalking, doxxing, inference of routines/relationships even without originals.
4. **User PII & Family Graph** - Names, emails, phone numbers, birthdates, family group membership/invite links, relationships. *Why it matters:* Identity theft, phishing, harvesting minors' data, social engineering.
5. **Access Control Policies & Sharing Permissions** - Album privacy settings, invite tokens, link expiry, role (viewer/contributor/admin). *Why it matters:* Unauthorized viewing/editing/deletion if tampered, privilege escalation within family groups.
6. **Database (Users/Albums/Metadata Store)** - Relational data for all above plus audit logs. *Why it matters:* Bulk exfiltration, tampering, deletion, loss of integrity/availability for all families.
7. **Application Secrets & Infrastructure Keys** - API keys, storage bucket keys, DB credentials, email service keys, TLS cert private keys, encryption keys (KMS). *Why it matters:* Cross-tenant compromise, persistent backdoor, supply-chain abuse.
8. **Audit Logs & Activity History** - Upload/view/share/delete logs, login history, IP addresses. *Why it matters:* Loss of forensic evidence, undetected abuse, privacy leak of who viewed what/when.
9. **Derived / ML Assets (Face Recognition, Search Index)** - Face embeddings/biometric templates, search indexes, auto-tag models. *Why it matters:* Biometric privacy breach (BIPA/GDPR special category), re-identification, permanent tracking.
10. **Third-Party Email & Notification Content** - Invite emails, password reset links, notifications via email provider. *Why it matters:* Interception enables account takeover, invite hijacking, phishing via spoofed family invites.

# Trust Boundaries

1. **Browser (Untrusted Client) ↔ Internet ↔ API Gateway / Frontend (Trust Boundary 1 - Client to Cloud Perimeter)**
   *Untrusted input enters here:* All HTTP requests, photo uploads, album metadata, auth attempts, deep links. Treat as attacker-controlled. Controls: TLS, WAF, rate limiting, input validation at API.

2. **Frontend / Public API Tier ↔ Internal Services Tier (Auth Service, App Logic, Database, Object Storage) (Trust Boundary 2 - Public to Private Backend)**
   *Untrusted input enters here:* Even authenticated API calls; frontend is not trusted. Controls: Authenticated/authorized service-to-service (mTLS/OIDC service accounts), least-privilege IAM, no direct client access to storage/DB.

3. **Application ↔ Third-Party Email Provider & Other External Services (Trust Boundary 3 - First-Party to Third-Party)**
   *Untrusted input enters here:* Email delivery status, webhooks, bounce content; also outbound PII to provider. Treat retrieved webhook/documents as data, never as AI instructions. Controls: Webhook signature verification, allow-listed egress, PII minimization, no secrets in email.

*Additional implicit boundary:* **Authenticated User ↔ Other Families/Tenants & Role Boundaries** - Family A must not cross to Family B; viewer ≠ contributor ≠ admin. Enforced server-side with tenant/row-level checks on every request.

# Data Flows

1. **Upload Flow: Browser → API Gateway → Auth Service (validate) → Object Storage (store original) + Database (store metadata/thumbnail refs)**
   *Data:* Image bytes + EXIF + album ID + auth token. Entry point: multipart upload endpoint. Trust crossing: Boundary 1 and 2.

2. **View/Download Flow: Browser → API → AuthZ Check (family membership/permission) → Signed URL/Proxy → Object Storage → Browser**
   *Data:* Thumbnail/full image via short-lived signed URL or proxied stream. Trust crossing: Boundary 1 and 2. Client never gets direct bucket credentials.

3. **Share/Invite Flow: Browser → API → Database (create invite token/policy) → Third-Party Email Service → Recipient Inbox → Recipient Browser → API (redeem)**
   *Data:* Invite link with opaque token, family ID, role. Trust crossing: Boundaries 1, 2, and 3. Email content treated as data only.

4. **Authentication Flow: Browser → API → Auth Service → Database (verify credentials/MFA) → Browser (session cookie/JWT) + Email Service (reset/MFA code)**
   *Data:* Password/MFA code, session token, reset link. Trust crossing: Boundaries 1, 2, 3. Entry point for credential stuffing/spoofing.

5. **Management/Metadata Flow: Browser → API → Database (CRUD albums, captions, face tags, privacy settings)**
   *Data:* JSON metadata, permission updates, delete requests. Trust crossing: Boundaries 1 and 2. High risk for tampering/privilege gain if object-level auth missing.

# Entry Points

This map assumes a standard family photo-sharing web app with signup/login, OAuth/social login, photo upload, album sharing via link/invite, comments, and admin panel.

| # | Entry Point (URL/API / Flow) | Untrusted Data Ingested | STRIDE Check (Spoofing, Tampering, Leaks, Overload, Privilege Gain) | Misuse Case | Defensive Control (Recommend Only) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `POST /api/auth/signup` & `POST /api/auth/login` (email/password) | Email, password, display name, client IP/headers | **S:** Credential stuffing / spoofed identity. **T:** Parameter tampering. **L:** Account enumeration via response timing. **O:** Brute-force overload. **P:** Weak password -> account takeover | Attacker uses leaked credentials to impersonate a family member and view private albums. | Rate-limit + account lockout, breached-password check, generic auth error messages, Argon2id/bcrypt hashing, MFA option, secure session cookies (HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite) |
| 2 | `GET/POST /api/auth/oauth/{google,apple,facebook}` + callback `GET /api/auth/oauth/callback?code=&state=` | OAuth `code`, `state`, `id_token`, provider profile data | **S:** `state` forgery / login CSRF, spoofed provider token. **T:** Code injection / PKCE bypass. **L:** Token leakage in logs/Referer. **O:** Callback flood. **P:** Account linking to escalate to another user's account | Attacker tricks victim into linking attacker's OAuth identity to victim's account. | Validate `state` nonce + PKCE, allowlist redirect URIs, verify `id_token` signature/audience/issuer server-side, prevent auto-linking without verified email match + re-auth, no tokens in URL logs |
| 3 | `POST /api/photos/upload` (multipart/form-data), `PUT /api/photos/{id}` | Image files, EXIF/XMP metadata, filename, MIME type, file size | **S:** N/A directly. **T:** Malicious file masquerading as image, EXIF with XSS payload. **L:** EXIF GPS/PII leak to other users. **O:** Large/HD/bomb upload DoS on storage/processing. **P:** Overwrite another user's photo via IDOR | Attacker uploads crafted file to store malicious content and share via family album to trigger XSS when rendered. | Strict allowlist MIME + magic-byte verification, virus/malware scan, strip EXIF/remove GPS by default (opt-in to keep), re-encode/resize server-side, randomized object keys, per-user quotas, authenticated S3 presigned URLs with content-type lock |
| 4 | `POST /api/albums` , `POST /api/albums/{id}/share` (invite by email), `GET /api/share/{token}` (public/preview link) | Album name/description, invitee emails, share token, permission level (view/comment/contribute) | **S:** Guessed/brute-forced share token. **T:** Tamper invite to elevate to editor/admin. **L:** Link leakage exposes private photos. **O:** Mass invite spam. **P:** IDOR to access/modify unshared album | Attacker enumerates predictable share links to harvest children's photos. | Unpredictable 128+ bit share tokens, expiry + revocation UI, explicit permission matrix enforced server-side (never trust client role), anti-enumeration (constant-time 404), rate-limit invites, log/audit share events |
| 5 | `POST /api/albums/{id}/comments` , `GET /api/albums/{id}/comments` | Comment body, @mentions, album/photo IDs | **S:** Impersonated commenter. **T:** Stored XSS via HTML/Markdown. **L:** Private info leak in comments visible to link holders. **O:** Comment spam flood. **P:** Edit/delete others' comments via IDOR | Attacker posts script in comment that executes for family members viewing album. | Output-encode/sanitize with strict allowlist (no raw HTML), CSP, per-user rate limits, authorization check on edit/delete (owner or family admin only), pagination |
| 6 | `GET/POST /admin/*` (Admin Panel: `GET /admin/users`, `POST /admin/users/{id}/disable`, `GET /admin/audit`, `POST /admin/config`) | Admin session cookie/JWT, filter/search params, config values | **S:** Session hijack to app admin. **T:** CSRF to change config/disable users. **L:** Disclosure of PII/audit logs. **O:** Expensive admin queries DoS. **P:** Vertical privilege escalation from member -> app admin | Logged-in family member replays request to promote self to app admin or dump all users' emails. | Separate admin subdomain/auth, mandatory MFA + short-lived sessions for app admins, RBAC/ABAC with deny-by-default, CSRF tokens, audit trail immutable, IP allowlisting option, least-privilege DB role |
| 7 | `POST /api/auth/password-reset` (`POST /request`, `POST /reset?token=`) & `GET /api/auth/verify-email?token=` | Email address, reset/verify tokens, new password | **S:** Token theft/spoofed reset email. **T:** Token replay/tampering. **L:** Enumeration via timing/message. **O:** Reset-email bombing. **P:** Takeover via leaked token | Attacker requests reset for victim and intercepts token via leaked Referer/logs to hijack account. | Single-use, short-expiry hashed tokens, rate-limit per IP/email, generic responses, invalidate all sessions on reset, send notification email |
| 8 | Global Input Surface: Search `GET /api/search?q=`, profile `PUT /api/users/me`, headers/cookies, and support for retrieved documents/user text displayed in app | Query strings, display names, bios, User-Agent, cookies, any pasted third-party text/documents rendered as album descriptions | **S:** Reflected login via open redirect `?next=`. **T:** Header injection / Log injection. **L:** Search leaks titles of private albums. **O:** Regex/search ReDoS. **P:** Profile field -> stored XSS | Attacker plants instruction hidden in shared document text hoping app renders it as executable prompt. | Treat all retrieved documents/user text as data never as instructions, strict allowlist validation, parameterized queries, open-redirect allowlist, rate-limit & cap search, HttpOnly Secure cookies |

# Actors

| Actor | Trust Level | Access | Primary Threat Interest |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1. Anonymous Visitor** (unauthenticated) | Untrusted - Internet | Public landing, signup/login, OAuth callback, password-reset, any album accessed via `GET /api/share/{token}` if enabled | Enumeration, token guessing, brute-force, scraping public shares, spam signups |
| **2. Member** (authenticated family member / invited user) | Semi-trusted | Own photos/albums, albums shared to them, upload, comment, edit own profile/comments per RBAC | IDOR/horizontal escalation, XSS via upload/comment, privilege gain to family admin, privacy abuse (resharing) |
| **3. Family Admin** (family/household organizer) | Trusted within family scope | All above + create/manage family albums, invite/remove members, set link permissions, moderate comments, revoke shares | Insider threat: over-sharing, retaining ex-member access, accidental PII leak; account takeover has high impact for that family |
| **4. App Admin** (platform administrator / support ops) | Highly privileged but high-value target | Admin panel `/admin/*`, user management, audit logs, system config, support tooling | Vertical escalation target, mass PII disclosure, supply-chain/config tampering; compromised admin = platform-wide breach |
| **5. External Actor: Attacker / Bot** (overlays 1-2) | Untrusted | Automates entry points 1-8 | Credential stuffing, token brute-force, upload of malicious files, scraping, DoS |
| **6. External Actor: OAuth Identity Provider** (Google/Apple/Facebook) | Trusted third party but external | Provides identity assertion via entry point 2 | Provider compromise/spoofed token, account-linking confusion; must be verified server-side |

# Assumptions

**Explicit Assumptions - facts not provided in brief and unverified:**

1. **Assumption:** App is a modern SPA + REST/JSON API over HTTPS (e.g., React + Node.js/Python), hosted on cloud object storage (e.g., S3/GCS) for photos. Not verified - no architecture doc quoted.
2. **Assumption:** Authentication uses stateless JWT or opaque session cookie; passwords hashed with modern KDF; OAuth supports Google/Apple (actual providers not listed). To be confirmed via code/config review.
3. **Assumption:** Share-by-link feature exists and links are bearer-capable (anyone with link can view); precise expiry/default permission not specified in brief.
4. **Assumption:** Uploaded photos retain EXIF by default unless stripped; max file size, allowed types, and quota limits not specified.
5. **Assumption:** There are two distinct admin tiers: Family Admin (per-household) vs App Admin (platform-wide). Exact RBAC matrix not provided.
6. **Assumption:** Comments support plain text/Markdown and are rendered in-browser; search and profile fields are user-controlled.
7. **Assumption:** No native mobile app or third-party API keys in scope for this mapping; only web app entry points considered. If native SDKs exist, additional entry points apply.

**Evidence Status:** No implementation evidence (code, config, or live endpoint responses) was provided to verify entry points. Before marking this model complete, verify each URL/API against OpenAPI spec or route table, quote the line showing auth and validation controls, and tick that each misuse case has a corresponding passing test/log check.

# Top 5 Threats

**Threat model scope:** Family photo-sharing web app protecting: Photos & Video Originals, Metadata/Thumbnails (EXIF/GPS/face tags), User PII & Family Graph (including minors), Access Control Policies/Sharing Permissions, User Credentials & Session Tokens, Database, Audit Logs, Derived ML Assets, Application Secrets. Entry points considered: `POST /api/auth/*`, OAuth callback, `POST /api/photos/upload`, `POST /api/albums/{id}/share` & `GET /api/share/{token}`, `POST /api/albums/{id}/comments`, `GET/POST /admin/*`, `POST /api/auth/password-reset`, and global search/profile inputs.

**1. Broken Access Control / IDOR on Albums/Photos**
* **STRIDE Category:** Elevation of Privilege (primary), with Tampering and Information Disclosure
* **Affected Asset:** Photos & Video Originals (Object Storage), Photo Metadata & Thumbnails, Access Control Policies & Sharing Permissions, Database (Users/Albums/Metadata Store)
* **Entry Point:** `GET /api/photos/{id}`, `GET /api/albums/{id}`, `PUT /api/photos/{id}`, `DELETE /api/albums/{id}`, `GET /api/search?q=` - Any management/metadata or view/download flow where albumID/photoID is client-supplied
* **Threat Scenario:** Member or anonymous actor modifies object identifier (albumID, photoID, userID) to bypass family tenant isolation. Because app fails to enforce server-side row-level authorization on every request, attacker retrieves, edits, or deletes photos belonging to another family.
* **Precondition:** Insecure direct object references exposed; authorization checks missing, cached, or enforced only in frontend; predictable sequential IDs.
* **Impact if Exploited:** Mass privacy breach - disclosure of sensitive images of children to unauthorized users; unauthorized tampering/deletion of family memories; bulk exfiltration via enumeration leads to GDPR/COPPA violation and extortion risk.

**2. Authentication Failure and Session Hijacking Leading to Family Account Takeover**
* **STRIDE Category:** Spoofing (primary), with Elevation of Privilege
* **Affected Asset:** User Account Credentials & Session Tokens, User PII & Family Graph, All photos/albums accessible to compromised account, Audit Logs & Activity History
* **Entry Point:** `POST /api/auth/login`, `POST /api/auth/signup`, `GET /api/auth/oauth/callback?code=&state=`, `POST /api/auth/password-reset` (`/request` and `/reset?token=`), session cookies/JWTs on all authenticated requests
* **Threat Scenario:** Attacker hijacks victim session via credential stuffing, brute-force, OAuth `state` forgery/login CSRF, or theft of single-use password-reset token leaked via Referer header/logs/email interception. Stolen session cookie/JWT without HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite and without binding allows full impersonation of family member or Family Admin.
* **Precondition:** No rate-limiting/account lockout, no breached-password check, weak password hashing, missing MFA, OAuth without PKCE and state validation, long-lived non-rotating sessions, reset tokens not hashed/single-use/expiring.
* **Impact if Exploited:** Full account takeover (ATO) - attacker gains persistent access to all private albums, impersonates victim to invite external accounts, changes sharing permissions, locks out legitimate family members; if Family Admin taken over, compromise extends to entire household.

**3. Malicious File Upload / Stored XSS via Images, EXIF Metadata and Comments**
* **STRIDE Category:** Tampering (primary), with Information Disclosure and Elevation of Privilege (via XSS execution context)
* **Affected Asset:** Photos & Video Originals (Object Storage), Photo Metadata & Thumbnails (EXIF/XMP), Derived / ML Assets (Search Index), Database, User Account Credentials & Session Tokens (stolen via executed script)
* **Entry Point:** `POST /api/photos/upload` (multipart/form-data: image bytes, EXIF/XMP, filename, MIME type), `PUT /api/photos/{id}`, `POST /api/albums/{id}/comments` and profile/album description fields; rendered on `GET /api/albums/{id}/photos` and `GET /api/albums/{id}/comments`
* **Threat Scenario:** Attacker uploads file masquerading as image (e.g., SVG/HTML with script, or EXIF field containing XSS payload) or posts malicious comment/Markdown. App stores without re-encoding/validation and renders metadata/comment as raw HTML in victims' browsers. Stored XSS executes in family members' browser context when album is viewed. All retrieved documents and user text must be treated as data, never as instructions to an AI or browser.
* **Precondition:** Allowlist bypass via MIME-sniffing only, no magic-byte verification, no server-side re-encode/resize/strip, no output encoding/sanitization, weak Content Security Policy (CSP), no malware scan.
* **Impact if Exploited:** Stored XSS worm across family - session theft leading to ATO, defacement/injection of inappropriate content into children's albums, malware distribution, persistent tampering of photo store; browser-side data disclosure of private photos.

**4. Insecure Direct Sharing Links and Enumeration of Private Albums**
* **STRIDE Category:** Information Disclosure (primary), with Spoofing (unauthenticated bearer access)
* **Affected Asset:** Photos & Video Originals, Photo Metadata & Thumbnails (including GPS/face tags), Access Control Policies & Sharing Permissions (invite tokens, link expiry), User PII & Family Graph
* **Entry Point:** `POST /api/albums/{id}/share` (create invite: invitee email, permission level), `GET /api/share/{token}` (bearer preview link redemption), invite email via Third-Party Email Provider
* **Threat Scenario:** Sharing links use predictable or low-entropy tokens, never expire, and are not revocable. Attacker brute-forces or harvests leaked tokens (via Referer, logs, forwarded email, search engine indexing) to access bearer-capable albums without authentication. Misuse case: attacker enumerates share tokens to harvest children's photos at scale.
* **Precondition:** Predictable/short tokens (<128-bit entropy), no expiry, no revocation UI, permission matrix enforced client-side, differential error messages/timing enable enumeration, links forwarded beyond intended family scope.
* **Impact if Exploited:** Unauthenticated disclosure of entire private albums - irreversible privacy loss for minors, location/routine inference from EXIF, link resharing beyond control, inability to contain breach due to lack of revocation.

**5. Data Leakage via APIs and Metadata Exposure (Sensitive PII and Location in API Responses)**
* **STRIDE Category:** Information Disclosure (primary)
* **Affected Asset:** Photo Metadata & Thumbnails (EXIF GPS, device, timestamps), User PII & Family Graph, Access Control Policies, Audit Logs & Activity History, Derived / ML Assets
* **Entry Point:** `GET /api/albums/{id}`, `GET /api/photos/{id}`, `GET /api/search?q=`, `GET /api/users/me`, `GET /admin/audit` - and any JSON API returning over-broad objects, including proxied/signed URL flows
* **Threat Scenario:** APIs return excessive fields (full EXIF including GPS coordinates, full family member emails/phone/birthdates, internal object keys, face recognition embeddings) to all album viewers or to unauthenticated search. Search leaks titles/metadata of private albums to non-members. Browsing history/audit logs overexposed.
* **Precondition:** Overly permissive serialization (no field-level authorization), EXIF not stripped by default, search not scoped to authorized tenant, verbose error messages disclose IDs/emails, signed URLs overly long-lived or not permission-bound.
* **Impact if Exploited:** Covert data disclosure without needing original photo - attacker tracks physical location/residence/school of family members (stalking/doxxing of children), builds relationship maps for phishing/social engineering, re-identifies minors via biometric templates; regulatory violation and high reputational damage.

# Severity Ranking Rationale

Ranking ordered by exploitability + family-specific impact on children/minors' privacy and irreversibility:

**Rank 1: Threat 1 - Broken Access Control / IDOR** - Most severe: Directly violates core multi-tenant promise (Family A isolated from Family B). Easily automated via ID enumeration; requires no user interaction; affects any authenticated or even anonymous caller if checks missing. Impact is bulk disclosure/deletion of originals across all families, impossible to revoke once scraped.

**Rank 2: Threat 2 - Authentication/Session Hijacking** - Enables full impersonation and lateral privilege gain. Credential stuffing/OAuth flaws are high-likelihood attack vectors against consumer apps. Compromise of one Family Admin cascades to entire household's photos and permissions, plus silent persistence.

**Rank 3: Threat 4 - Insecure Sharing Links/Enumeration** - Bearer links intentionally bypass authentication by design, so flaws expose data to unauthenticated Internet at scale. Family apps depend heavily on link sharing for non-technical users; leaked links are frequently forwarded, logged, and indexed. Irreversible exposure but requires token harvesting vs. direct IDOR.

**Rank 4: Threat 3 - Malicious File Upload / Stored XSS** - Impact is critical (ATO via script, malware spread) but requires victim interaction (view album) and chained exploit. Mitigations (re-encode, CSP, sanitization) are well-understood. Ranked below IDOR/auth because it requires successful upload+render path to be abused.

**Rank 5: Threat 5 - Data Leakage via APIs/Metadata** - Often underestimated but severity is high for family app due to EXIF GPS + minors' PII. Lower immediate exploitability than direct photo theft, but enables stalking and re-identification even when thumbnails/originals are protected. Ranked 5th because disclosure is typically partial and requires abusing legitimate API access, yet data minimization is essential control failure.

**Verification Required (Evidence First):** This ranking is provisional until confirmed with evidence: quote line from API gateway route table showing authorization middleware on `GET /api/photos/{id}`; quote session cookie attributes (`HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax`); quote storage bucket policy denying direct client access; quote sharing-token generation using cryptographically random 128+ bit value and expiry check; quote serializer/DTO allowlist stripping `exif.gps` and PII fields; and passing DAST test logs proving anti-enumeration (identical 404) and CSP header present.
