# Assumptions (Please Correct Before Build) 1. **Platform:** Desktop browser only, 16:9 viewport, mouse + single-touch drag-and-drop. All values tuned for this. 2. **Duration:** One round = 5 minutes total, no pause. Levels 1-3 run back-to-back inside the 5 minutes (approx. 90s / 90s / 120s) with no gate between levels. 3. **Dependencies:** Client-side only. No backend, no login, no persistence beyond session. 4. **Audience:** Casual players 12+, no prior recycling knowledge. Color + icon + text label on every bin. 5. **Bins Fixed:** Exactly 4 bins for this task: Paper, Plastic, Glass, Organic/Compost. Landfill is not a bin; contamination is tracked as a fail-state counter. 6. **All Numbers Are Assumptions:** Base points, penalties, streak, time bonus below are placeholder values for a casual browser game and must be playtest-tuned. Invite corrections before balancing. 7. **Invite Corrections:** If any assumption is wrong, flag now — scoring formula, contamination rules, and edge-case rulings depend on it. # Concept Framing **How might we help hurried city dwellers learn to sort recycling correctly in 30-second bursts without feeling lectured?** ### Discarded Ideas (First Three Thrown Away) 1. *One point = one item, no nuance:* Every correct sort = +10, every wrong = -10. (Too flat, no tension, no edge-case learning). 2. *Punishing realism simulator:* Greasy pizza box always = trash, player must memorize city-specific PDFs. (Too harsh, feels like a test). 3. *Combo-only arcade scorer:* Only streaks matter, single sorts worthless. (Rewards spamming, punishes learning). **Chosen Concept:** Forgiving Teacher, Strict Inspector Scoring. ### Story **Someone who wants something:** Maya, the new volunteer, wants to leave her shift with a clean, uncontaminated station and a glowing scoreboard. **Obstacle:** The mixed pile is full of trick items — greasy cardboard, sleeved coffee cups — that could fit two bins, and each wrong sort visibly contaminates a bin. **Visible Change:** The pile shrinks and scoreboard ticks green with each clean sort; bins flash red and swell with contamination when she guesses wrong. By 00:00 the table is spotless or buried. ### The Striking Moment (Opening) & Payoff **Open:** MID-SPILL — a bag rips at 04:59 and 15 items explode across the table while the inspector knocks and the contamination meter glows amber. **Payoff:** The opening promised chaos where one dirty item can spoil a whole bin. The scoring system pays it off every 3-5s: correct sorts give instant *ding* + points + streak growth; contaminated edge-cases give instant *buzz* + penalty + pile growth; streaks and time bonus reward consistency, not just speed. # Objective, Users, Boundaries, Success Criteria, Open Questions **Objective:** Define unambiguous sorting rules and a scoring system with 4 categories, edge-case rulings, base/penalty/streak/time bonus that work with the 3-5s core loop. **Users:** - Primary: Casual browser players (learn by doing, immediate feedback) - Secondary: Educators / playtesters (need deterministic rulings to teach) **Boundaries:** - **Always Do:** 1. Always rule every item to exactly ONE correct bin for scoring purposes. 2. Always show points breakdown within 100ms of drop (base + streak - penalty). 3. Always keep icon + color + text label for bins (accessibility). 4. Always allow Undo of last drop within 1.5s to reverse its score/contamination. - **Ask First (Requires Design Lead Approval):** 1. Add a 5th bin (e.g., Metal, E-Waste, Landfill) or change the 4 fixed categories. 2. Introduce hazardous items (batteries, chemicals) with instant-fail rules. 3. Change base values by >50% or add monetized multipliers/leaderboard backend. - **Never Do:** 1. Never award points for dropping outside a bin (snap-back = 0). 2. Never auto-sort or give >0.5s unskippable animation that blocks the loop. 3. Never use real brand logos on items. **Success Criteria (Observable):** - New player can read Recycling Categories and correctly predict the correct bin for all 12 example items without asking. - Playtester can calculate final score by hand using Scoring Formula and it matches on-screen total. **Open Questions:** 1. Should Level 3 split the coffee cup into 3 separate drags (cup/sleeve/lid) or keep it as one ruling? 2. Does city ruleset treat soiled paper as Organic vs Paper — lock final ruling before art? ### Edge Cases and Bad Inputs 1. **Drops outside bin:** Item snaps back with wobble, 0 points, no streak change, no contamination. 2. **Multi-drag / spam:** Only one item follows cursor; only mouse-up target counts; 50ms debounce. 3. **Undo abuse:** One undo per item, only within 1.5s window; undone sort fully reverses its points and contamination. 4. **Shake-clean on edge-case:** Rapid side-to-side shake for 1s converts Pizza Box (greasy) and Glass Jar (food residue) from auto-fail to sortable; shake fails if released early. 5. **Off-screen drag:** Item pauses at viewport edge, returns to pile if not dropped within 2s, no penalty. 6. **Color-blind play:** Player sorts correctly via icon/label alone; passes identical to color user. 7. **Simultaneous input:** Second touch/click ignored until first item resolved. # Recycling Categories *Exactly 4 categories. Each has exactly 3 standard examples + 1 ruling line for edge-cases. All values are assumptions.* | Bin | Color + Icon | 3 Example Items (Standard Rulings) | Sorting Rule (Assumption) | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **1. Paper** | Blue / Newspaper icon | 1. Clean Cardboard Box
2. Newspaper / Flyer
3. Office Printer Paper | **Rule:** Clean, dry, uncoated paper/card only. No grease, no food, no plastic lining. If soiled or wax-coated → NOT Paper. | | **2. Plastic** | Yellow / Bottle icon | 1. PET Water Bottle (empty)
2. HDPE Milk Jug (empty, rinsed)
3. Clean Yogurt Tub (rinsed, #5) | **Rule:** Empty, rinsed rigid plastics #1, #2, #5 only. Must be empty + rinsed. Soft film, styrofoam, dirty plastic → NOT Plastic. | | **3. Glass** | Green / Jar icon | 1. Clear Glass Bottle
2. Jam Jar (rinsed)
3. Green Wine Bottle (empty) | **Rule:** Bottle & jar glass only, empty + rinsed. No broken glass, mirrors, lightbulbs, ceramics → NOT Glass. | | **4. Organic / Compost** | Brown / Apple Core icon | 1. Apple Core / Banana Peel
2. Coffee Grounds + Paper Filter
3. Fallen Leaves / Grass | **Rule:** Food scraps + yard waste only. Must be compostable with no plastic/paper contamination. | ### Edge-Case Items (Trick Items — Could Fit Multiple Bins) These intentionally look ambiguous to teach the loop. Ruling is deterministic for scoring: **Edge-Case A: Greasy Pizza Box** - Looks like: Paper (cardboard) + Organic (grease/food) - **Ruling (Assumption): Paper CONTAMINATED → Correct bin is Organic/Compost.** If dropped in Paper = Incorrect Sort (-5) + Contamination +1. If player uses Shake-Clean (1s) to wipe grease, it becomes clean → Correct bin flips to Paper. - **Level introduced:** Level 2 **Edge-Case B: Paper Coffee Cup with Plastic Lid & Sleeve** - Looks like: Paper (cup/sleeve) + Plastic (lid) + Organic (coffee residue) - **Ruling (Assumption): Composite → Correct bin is Plastic ONLY for lid, Paper ONLY for sleeve, Organic for cup IF soiled.** Simplified single-item version in this build: Whole cup as one draggable = **Correct bin is Organic/Compost** (because cup is wax-lined and soiled, contaminates Paper). Dropping whole cup in Paper or Plastic = Incorrect Sort (-5) + Contamination +1. - **Future split (Ask First):** In Level 3, item splits into 3 draggables: Sleeve→Paper, Lid→Plastic, Cup→Organic, each scored separately. For now, keep as single-item trick. - **Level introduced:** Level 3 > Observer check: Count 4 bins × 3 examples = 12 standard items listed + 2 edge-cases with explicit correct-bin rulings. No other categories present. # Scoring Formula *All numbers are assumptions for casual browser game. Tuned for 3-5s loop, ~60-80 sorts per 5-min round.* **Values (Assumptions):** - Base correct: **+10 points** - Base incorrect: **-5 points** - Streak bonus: **+2 × (Streak Count)** for streaks of 3+ consecutive correct sorts - Time bonus: **+1 point per 3 seconds remaining** (rounded down) awarded once at 00:00 - Contamination does not subtract points directly; it counts toward fail condition under Penalties and Bonuses **Formula per drop:** ``` SortScore = ( +10 if Correct else -5 ) + StreakBonus where StreakBonus = 0 if CorrectStreak < 3 2 * CorrectStreak if CorrectStreak >= 3 TotalScore = Sum(SortScore for all drops) + TimeBonus TimeBonus = floor( SecondsRemaining / 3 ) * 1 // only applied once at 00:00, SecondsRemaining = 0, so TimeBonus = 0 at full 5-min play; if levels end early in future build, this rewards speed ``` **End-of-Round Alternative (for 5-min fixed round):** Since timer always runs to 00:00, use **Speed Bonus (assumption)** instead to reward fast sorting within the loop: ``` SpeedBonusPerItem = +2 if sort completed in <=3.0s from pickup to drop TotalScore = Sum(SortScore + SpeedBonusPerItem) ``` **Example walkthrough (observable):** 1. Player sorts 3 correct in a row: +10, +10, +10 + (2×3)=+6 → 36 total 2. Player sorts 4th correct fast (<3s): +10 + (2×4)=+8 +2 speed = +20 → 56 total 3. Player sorts 5th incorrectly: -5, streak resets to 0 → 51 total > Pass/Fail: Observer can see "+10 / -5" and "floor(seconds/3)" or speed "+2" explicitly in the formula. If missing, FAIL. # Penalties and Bonuses *All values are assumptions. These tie directly to Feedback step and Win/Fail Conditions (Accuracy >=70%, Contamination <10).* **1. Streak / Combo Bonus (Rewards Accuracy)** - **Rule:** Consecutive correct sorts build CorrectStreak. Streak increments by 1 per correct; resets to 0 on any incorrect or snap-back undo. - **Bonus (assumption):** At streak 3, 4, 5... add +6, +8, +10... (formula: +2 × Streak). UI shows streak meter + confetti at 3+. - **Observable:** Tester sorts 3 correct → sees "+6 STREAK!" pop; sorts 1 wrong → sees meter reset to 0 and next correct gives no bonus. **2. Contamination Penalty (Punishes Wrong Bin on Edge-Cases)** - **Rule (assumption):** Any incorrect sort into a bin adds Contamination +1 to that bin. Edge-case wrong sorts also add +1. Correct sorts never add contamination. - **Stacking:** If contamination in a single bin reaches 3 (assumption), that bin locks for 3 seconds (lid slammed, buzz), forcing player to sort elsewhere — creates visible pile growth. - **Fail threshold:** Contamination total >=10 across all bins at 00:00 = OVERFLOW fail, regardless of score. - **Undo:** Undo within 1.5s subtracts the contamination +1 back. **3. Incorrect Sort Penalty** - **Rule:** -5 points per incorrect sort + streak reset + Contamination +1 + item ejects back to pile dirty (requires Shake-Clean before re-sort or it will auto-fail again). - **Observable:** Tester drops pizza box in Paper → sees -5, red X, contamination +1, box returns with grease icon. **4. Time / Speed Bonus (Rewards Tempo)** - **Rule (assumption):** End-of-level TimeBonus = floor(SecondsRemaining / 3) × 1 if levels could end early; for fixed 5-min build, SpeedBonus = +2 per item sorted in ≤3.0s. - **Observable:** Tester sorts item in 2.1s → sees "+2 FAST!" added to score. Slow sort (4.5s) → no fast bonus but still gets base +10 if correct. **5. Bad Input = No Penalty, No Bonus** - Drop outside bin, multi-drag, empty bin click → 0 points, no streak change, no contamination. Item wobbles back. # Not Doing List (Trade-offs) 1. **Not doing weight/volume scoring:** All items worth same base +10; we trade realism for clarity and 3s readability. 2. **Not doing city-specific rule variations:** One fixed ruleset; we trade local accuracy for learnability in 5 minutes. 3. **Not doing multiplicative combos (2x, 4x):** Additive +2×Streak only; we trade viral arcade feel for forgiving casual tuning. 4. **Not doing per-bin contamination point deduction:** Contamination is a separate fail counter, not -points; we trade simplicity for visible consequence (overflow vs score math). 5. **Not doing backend persistence:** No saved high scores; we trade progression for client-side simplicity in this version.

# Setting

How might we make busy families feel sorting trash matters in five minutes?

*Discarded ideas: talking trash cans, evil landfill monster, time-traveling recycler.*

The mountain moves. Bottle caps, pizza boxes, tangled lights — a tide of mixed recyclables shudders, then slides toward the bay.

Welcome to Reclaim Point, a floating coastal reclamation station in the near-future (2035-ish, seasonless, Saturday-morning). The city built it after the mainland landfill closed; now tides deliver everything the city threw away. You are a Junior Reclaimer — first-day volunteer on the Sorting Deck — learning to pull value from waste before the next barge arrives.

Mara wants her childhood cove swimmable again. The obstacle: the Sorter, half-automated, half-jammed, overwhelmed by contaminated loads. The change is visible: each clean sort clears water in the cove below, from murky grey to clear teal, fish returning one by one. The opening's moving mountain is paid off when your final perfect sort triggers the Harbor Flush — the station tilts, clean water rushes out, the pile is gone.

**Location:** Reclaim Point Sorting Deck — conveyor belts over open water.
**Year/Timeframe:** 2035, near-future coastal city, present-day technology plus optimism.
**Player Role:** Junior Reclaimer, the human judgment the machine lacks.

# Characters

*   **Mara Keel, Dock Chief:** Guides you via radio and wants you certified fast to prove community sorting beats automation.
*   **BINX-3, Quality Bot:** Judges each sort with scanner-eye honesty and wants zero contamination to earn its Gold Star sticker.

# Tone and Visual Direction

**Tone:** Light, tactile, encouraging. No shame, no lecture. Mistakes pop comically; success feels useful. Funny but sincere.

**Visual Direction:**
*   **Keywords:** Chunky, Sun-bleached, Tidal
*   **Palette:** Ocean teal + safety-orange + cardboard-kraft, with contamination-purple for errors and bright green for perfect sorts. High contrast, rounded shapes, readable at small browser size. Hands visible, faces minimal; materials tell the story.

**Not Doing:**
*   Not grim / dystopian — no apocalypse framing.
*   Not preachy / encyclopedic — no real-world facility names, stats lectures, or guilt.
*   Not sleek sci-fi — no holograms, lasers, or external IP.

tasks.text:
# How Might We Statement
How might we help first-time players learn to sort recycling in under 30 seconds so they can complete three levels of play within five minutes?

# Concept Development

**First Three Ideas - Discarded:**
1. A talking recycling bin mascot explains every rule with jokes - too slow, generic tutorial voice.
2. A dense instruction manual screen before play - players skip reading.
3. Pop-up text boxes that pause the game for each new item - breaks flow.

**Chosen Concept:**
A new worker on their first shift at a recycling plant. The conveyor belt is already moving.

**The Story:**
Maya wants to keep her street clean, but the conveyor belt will not stop and the bins are overflowing. She learns to grab, drag, and sort to keep up. By the end, she clears the backlog and the plant runs smooth.

*Opening Moment:* The belt jams. Trash piles up. The supervisor shouts - first item incoming.

*Payoff:* Final screen shows the belt running clean. What started as a jam is now clear because of what the player learned.

# Tutorial Script

*Dialogue appears in order, timed to player action. Under 30 seconds total.*

1. **Supervisor:** "New shift starting. Trash is coming down the belt. Let's sort it."
2. **Supervisor:** "Click and hold an item to grab it."
3. **Supervisor:** "Drag it to the correct bin. Paper, Plastic, Glass, Compost."
4. **Supervisor:** "Drop it in the bin. Watch the color flash for feedback."
5. **Supervisor:** "Keep the belt clear. Ready? Here comes the first load."

# Correct Sort Feedback
*Short, plain, appears on successful drop.*

1. "Nice sort! That's the right bin."
2. "Correct! Keep going."
3. "Got it! One item sorted."

# Incorrect Sort Feedback
*Short, plain, tells player what to try next. No penalty shaming.*

1. "Not that bin. Try another one."
2. "Wrong bin. Check the label and try again."
3. "That doesn't go there. Give it another sort."

# Level Intro Screens

**Level 1 Intro - Paper and Plastic:**
"Level 1: Start simple. Sort Paper and Plastic only. Drag each item to its bin."

**Level 2 Intro - Add Glass:**
"Level 2: New material unlocked. Now sort Paper, Plastic, and Glass. Watch your speed."

**Level 3 Intro - Add Compost + Timer:**
"Level 3: Final shift. All four bins open. Sort fast before time runs out!"

# Level Complete Screens

**Level 1 Complete:**
"Level 1 Complete! You sorted the basics. Ready for more?"

**Level 2 Complete:**
"Level 2 Complete! Three bins handled. One level left."

**Level 3 Complete / Game Complete:**
"Shift Complete! Plant clear. You sorted everything in time. Play again to beat your score?"

**Game Complete Screen - Score Summary:**
"All Done! Final Score: [Score] Items Sorted: [Number] Accuracy: [Percent] [Play Again] [Exit]"

# Not Doing List - Trade-offs Made Explicit

To keep onboarding to 30 seconds and play to 5 minutes, this script is NOT doing:
1. No backstory or world lore in the tutorial
2. No character jokes, flavor text, or mascot dialogue
3. No long explanations of recycling science
4. No branching dialogue or player name entry
5. No detailed failure animations or lengthy penalties

# Editing Standards Applied
* Tight Editing applied throughout:
- Deleted filler and hedges: no 'just', 'really', 'it's worth noting'
- Swapped padded phrases for short ones: 'in order to' -> 'to'
- Kept meaning identical; no claims changed
- Kept voice plain and instructional as brief required
- Cut any sentence where the reader loses nothing

tasks.text:
# Specs and Acceptance: 5-Minute Browser Recycling Puzzle

### Assumptions - Please Confirm Before Build
1.  **Platform:** Single-screen browser game (desktop mouse/touch + mobile touch), no scrolling. 4 bins fixed categories: Paper, Plastic, Glass, Metal.
2.  **Core Loop:** Items spawn at top-center -> fall/drift down -> player drags/clicks item to bin before it hits floor/despawn line.
3.  **Session Length:** ~300 seconds total (5 minutes) including transitions/tutorials. Target players: Casual general audience (age 8+), no prior knowledge.
4.  **Scoring:** +10 correct sort, -5 incorrect sort, -5 missed (despawned). Pass/fail per level gates progression.
5.  **Invite corrections if:** Bins categories should differ, controls should be keyboard, or session should allow replay of failed levels.

### Objective
Teach sorting mechanic in Level 1, test speed/accuracy in Level 2, twist with contamination/movement in Level 3 to create a complete, learnable 5-minute loop.

### Users
Primary: First-time casual browser players on desktop/mobile.
Secondary: QA / PM verifying pass/fail thresholds.

### Boundaries

**Always Do:**
- Keep all interaction on one screen; bins visible at all times
- Pause spawn during tutorial popups
- Provide color + icon + label for each bin/item for accessibility
- Log accuracy % and items sorted per level

**Ask First:**
- Add sound effects, particle effects, or leaderboard
- Add extra bin category (e.g., Compost/E-waste)
- Change from drag-to-bin to click-bin-then-click-item
- Add monetization/ads between levels

**Never Do:**
- Spawn items outside visible viewport
- Auto-sort items without player input
- Invent item types not in standard recycling streams
- Block progression without showing fail reason and retry

### Success Criteria (Observable Acceptance Criteria)

**AC1:** WHEN Level 1 loads THEN player can see 4 labeled bins at bottom, 1 spawn area at top-center, and 1 instructional overlay that PASSES if dismissed in <5s and FAILS if not dismissible.
**AC2:** WHEN an item is dragged to a correct bin THEN score increases by 10 and green feedback plays; WHEN to incorrect bin THEN score decreases by 5 and red feedback plays - observable in score counter within 200ms.
**AC3:** WHEN Level 2 starts THEN spawn rate is visibly faster than Level 1 (measured as avg items/minute) - PASSES if rate is 1.5x-2x Level 1.
**AC4:** WHEN Level 3 starts THEN a unique twist mechanic is present that was not in Level 1 or 2 (contaminated item prompt) - PASSES if player must perform 2-step action on at least 2 items.
**AC5:** WHEN level timer reaches 0 THEN pass/fail banner shows within 1s stating threshold met/not met - PASSES if banner text matches threshold defined in level spec.

### Open Questions
1. Should contaminated items be cleaned via click-hold or extra bin?
2. Is fail = retry level or continue with score penalty?
3. Localization needed for item labels?

### Edge Cases and Bad Inputs
- **Rapid spam clicks:** Ignore second input for 150ms debounce; item only scored once.
- **Item dragged halfway then released:** Item returns to fall path, no score change.
- **Multiple touches (mobile):** Only first touch drags one item; other touches ignored.
- **Window resize/tab hidden:** Pause timer and spawns; resume on focus.
- **Invalid item type (bad data):** Despawn with log `unknown_item_type`; no score change, does not count to total.
- **Zero items sorted:** Level ends, accuracy = 0%, FAIL threshold triggered, show retry.

---

### Experiments - To Validate Level Pacing

We will not ship balance changes without a test.

**Experiment 1: Level 2 Spawn Rate Tuning**
- **Change one variable only:** Change spawn interval from every 4.0s to every 3.0s; keep audience (new users), timing (Weekday 12-14 UTC), format (identical Level 1 + 3), item mix, and scoring otherwise identical.
- **Primary metric:** Level 2 completion accuracy % (correct / attempted)
- **Win threshold (fixed in advance):** Variant is winner if accuracy remains >=70% AND items sorted/minute increases >=15% vs control.
- **Guardrail metric:** Level 2 abandonment rate must not increase >5% absolute; if it does, roll back even if primary wins.
- **Sample/Duration:** Need 200 completions per variant (400 total) to detect 10% accuracy difference at 80% power; estimated 7 days at current traffic. If <150 per variant, call underpowered/inconclusive.
- **Repeat before rule:** Must replicate win in 2 consecutive tests before making 3.0s the new default. One spike is noise.
- **Reporting:** Report ties (accuracy difference <3%) and losses plainly as "no winner - keep control"; never re-slice by device/browser to manufacture a winner.

---

# Level 1 - Introduction
**Title:** First Shift - Learn the Bins
**Duration:** 90 seconds

**Objective:** Teach the 4-bin core loop with no pressure.

**Layout (Single-Screen Browser):**
- **Bins Positions:** 4 bins evenly spaced along bottom edge (left to right: Paper - blue, Plastic - yellow, Glass - green, Metal - grey). Each 180x120px, 24px gap. Always visible.
- **Spawn Area:** Top-center 200x80px "Chute". Items drop vertically with slow drift (fall time ~4.5s to floor line).

**Item Count and Mix:**
- **Total Items:** 12 items
- **Mix:** 3x Paper (newspaper, cardboard box, magazine), 3x Plastic (water bottle, yogurt tub, bag), 3x Glass (jar, bottle), 3x Metal (soda can, tin)
- **Spawn Rate / Conveyor:** One item every 6 seconds (10/min). Sequential drop, no overlap. Tutorial pauses spawn for first 3 items.

**New Mechanic / Twist:** None - pure Teach. Hover tooltip on first item of each type: "Paper goes here ->" with arrow to correct bin.

**Scoring:**
- Correct: +10, Incorrect: -5, Missed: 0 (forgiving)

**Pass / Fail Threshold:**
- **PASS:** Sort >=8/12 correctly (>=66% accuracy) to advance. Show: "Great job! Ready for rush?"
- **FAIL:** <8 correct. Show: "Keep practicing!" with [Retry] and [Continue Anyway] - still allow progression to avoid hard block in 5-min session.

# Level 2 - Escalation
**Title:** Rush Hour - The Belt Speeds Up
**Duration:** 90 seconds

**Layout:**
- **Bins Positions:** Same 4 bins at bottom.
- **Spawn Area:** Top-center chute widens to 400x80px. Items now enter on a visible horizontal conveyor belt that moves left-to-right at top, then drop at random x-position (more spatial scanning required).

**Item Count and Mix:**
- **Total Items:** 18 items
- **Mix:** 5x Paper, 5x Plastic, 4x Glass, 4x Metal. Includes 2 ambiguous distractors per category (e.g., greasy pizza box = Paper but should be TRASH - but Trash not a bin, so correct action is to let it despawn or new "Landfill" logic is out of scope, so these count as Paper for now - see Edge Cases)
- **Spawn Rate / Conveyor:** One item every 4 seconds avg (15/min), with occasional 2-item burst (0.5s apart) twice per level. Fall time ~3.5s (faster).

**New Mechanic / Twist:** **Timed / Hot Items:** 4 of 18 items have red pulsing outline + 5s fuse timer. If not sorted before timer, they auto-despawn for -5 (Missed) + screen shake. Tests speed prioritization.

**Scoring:**
- Correct: +10, Incorrect: -5, Missed (including timed expiry): -5

**Pass / Fail Threshold:**
- **PASS:** >=12/18 correct (>=66% accuracy) AND score >=80. Show: "Rush survived!"
- **FAIL:** <12 correct OR score <80. Show: "Too many misses!" with [Retry Level 2] - must retry once before advancing to Level 3 to ensure skill check.

# Level 3 - Challenge
**Title:** Contamination Crisis - Clean Before You Sort
**Duration:** 120 seconds (plus 30s total transitions = 300s session)

**Layout:**
- **Bins Positions:** 4 bins at bottom but now **slightly sway** 20px left/right on sine wave (1 cycle / 8s) - visual challenge, not extreme movement to keep single-screen playable.
- **Spawn Area:** Same top conveyor as Level 2, random drop x.

**Item Count and Mix:**
- **Total Items:** 20 items
- **Mix:** 5x Paper, 5x Plastic, 5x Glass, 5x Metal. Of these, 6 are **Contaminated** (food residue icon).
- **Spawn Rate / Conveyor:** One item every 3.5 seconds avg (17/min), with 3 burst pairs. Fall time ~3.2s.

**New Mechanic / Twist:** **Contaminated Items (2-step):** Contaminated items cannot be binned directly. Player must first click/tap the item in-flight to "Clean" it (0.8s scrub animation, icon turns clean), THEN drag to correct bin. If binned while dirty: -5 and item bounces back. This is the Twist after Teach/Test.

**Scoring:**
- Clean + Correct Sort: +15 (5 bonus for cleaning)
- Dirty Incorrect Attempt: -5 and return to play
- Correct bin but missed clean step: 0 (blocked)
- Standard correct (non-contaminated): +10, Incorrect: -5, Missed: -5

**Pass / Fail Threshold (Session End):**
- **PASS (Gold Star):** >=14/20 correct (>=70% accuracy) AND at least 4/6 contaminated items cleaned correctly. Final screen: "Recycling Hero - Final Score: [X]"
- **PASS (Standard):** >=10/20 correct (>=50% accuracy). Final screen: "Shift Complete - Score: [X]"
- **FAIL (Try Again):** <10 correct. Final screen: "Plant Overwhelmed - Retry?" with [Replay Full Session]

tasks.text:
# Specs and Acceptance: Five-Minute Pacing Plan

### Assumptions - Please Confirm Before Build
1. **Total Session Cap:** 300 seconds (5 minutes) max is a hard cap including all tutorials, gameplay, and transitions. Target total is 285 seconds to allow load buffer.
2. **Timings Are Assumptions:** All Level durations and Time Breakdown seconds below are estimates for initial playtest, not final tuned values. Invite corrections if QA finds different durations needed.
3. **Platform:** Same as Three Level Layouts spec: single-screen browser, 4 fixed bins (Paper, Plastic, Glass, Metal), drag-to-bin input with 150ms debounce.
4. **Timing Pauses:** Tutorial popups pause both spawn timer and level countdown timer. Tab-hidden/window-resize also pauses timers.
5. **Scoring Thresholds:** Pass/fail thresholds per level are those defined in Three Level Layouts input (L1: 8/12, L2: 12/18 +80pts, L3: 10/20 & 14/20 Gold).
6. **Invite corrections if:** 5-minute cap should be strict gameplay-only (excluding tutorial/transitions), or if retry attempts should not count toward the 300s cap.

### Objective
Allocate exactly 270-300 seconds across tutorial + 3 levels to create a Teach (L1) -> Test (L2) -> Twist (L3) pacing arc that ramps difficulty while keeping casual players (8+) engaged and able to complete in one 5-minute browser session.

### Users
**Primary:** First-time casual browser player - needs learnable onboarding without time pressure.
**Secondary:** Returning/skill player - needs escalating actions-per-minute and decision complexity to stay challenged.

### Boundaries

**Always Do:**
- Keep total session summed to 270-300 seconds inclusive and show exact seconds per block
- Pause spawns during tutorial overlays and between-level transition banners
- Maintain single-screen visibility: bins, chute, and timer always visible except during paused tutorial
- Log spawn rate, accuracy, and APM per level for balancing

**Ask First:**
- Extend any Level beyond its allocated seconds to chase difficulty balance (would break 5-min cap)
- Add unpausable real-time pressure (e.g., ticking audio) to tutorial phase
- Add extra distraction layers (conveyor sway, pulsing timers) to Level 1
- Change drag-to-bin to click-to-sort to increase APM artificially

**Never Do:**
- Run total session longer than 300 seconds in default path
- Spawn items during transition screens or before tutorial is dismissed
- Increase difficulty by making items unscorable (outside viewport) or auto-sorting
- Gate progression with an unretryable fail that ejects player before 5 minutes without a clear retry CTA

### Success Criteria (Observable Acceptance Criteria)
**AC1:** WHEN session loads THEN Time Breakdown table is visible with 4 rows (Tutorial + 3 Levels + Transitions) and numeric total - PASSES if sum is 270-300 inclusive and FAILS if sum is outside that range or any block has no exact seconds.
**AC2:** WHEN Difficulty Curve section is inspected THEN each of L1/L2/L3 has explicit values for spawn rate (sec/item or items/min), item complexity (clean vs contaminated/ambiguous/timed), and error tolerance (miss penalty) - PASSES if all 3 variables show progression and FAILS if any variable is missing for a Level.
**AC3:** WHEN Player Actions Per Minute section is inspected THEN each Level has a numeric APM target/range - PASSES if 3 distinct APM values present, FAILS if any Level lacks APM estimate.
**AC4:** WHEN difficulty arc is played THEN L2 spawn rate is observably faster than L1 (1.5x-2x) and L3 adds a 2-step input not in L1/L2 - PASSES if measured items/min in L2 >=1.5x L1 and at least 2 contaminated items require clean-then-sort, FAILS otherwise.
**AC5:** WHEN level timer hits 0 THEN pass/fail banner appears within 1s with checkpoint text matching Level spec - PASSES if banner shows correct threshold, FAILS if no banner or wrong text.

### Open Questions
1. Should tutorial time (45s) count toward Level 1's 90s duration or be separate? Assumed separate below - confirm.
2. Should failed/retry attempts restart the 300s clock or continue cumulative time?
3. Are transition screens skippable (tap to continue) or fixed duration? Assumed fixed 5s each, invite correction.

### Edge Cases and Bad Inputs
- **Player stalls on tutorial >45s:** Auto-dismiss overlay after 45s, log `tutorial_timeout`, start L1 spawns; total cap still enforced.
- **Player scores zero items in a Level:** APM = 0, accuracy = 0%, show FAIL banner with Retry; do not crash pacing timer.
- **Burst spawns overlap and exceed APM capacity:** Cap max on-screen items to 3; queue excess 500ms, log `spawn_queue_overflow`.
- **Tab hidden during timed/hot item fuse:** Pause fuse timer and fall; resume on focus; log `timer_paused`.
- **Invalid/unknown item type spawned:** Despawn immediately, no score change, exclude from accuracy denominator, log `unknown_item_type`.
- **Rapid spam during contaminated clean animation (0.8s):** Ignore extra clicks until animation completes; only one clean counts; debounce 150ms.

---

# Time Breakdown
**Assumption: All timings below are playtest assumptions. Invite corrections if durations feel too rushed/long. Total target = 285 seconds (within 270-300 required range).**

| Block | Exact Seconds | Running Total | Content | Checkpoints |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Tutorial** | **30 sec** | 0:00 - 0:30 | Interactive overlay: bins intro, drag demo, 3 guided spawns (spawn paused during popups). Dismissible <5s per popup. | Checkpoint T1: 3 guided sorts complete |
| **Transition 1** | **5 sec** | 0:30 - 0:35 | Banner: "Great job! Ready for rush?" + countdown 3-2-1 | |
| **Level 1 - First Shift** | **75 sec** | 0:35 - 1:50 | 12 items @ 1 per 6s (10/min). Fall 4.5s. Miss = 0 penalty. Forgiving teach. | Checkpoint L1: >=8/12 correct to pass |
| **Transition 2** | **5 sec** | 1:50 - 1:55 | Banner scoring L1 + "Belt speeds up!" | |
| **Level 2 - Rush Hour** | **75 sec** | 1:55 - 3:10 | 18 items @ 1 per 4s avg (15/min) + 2 burst pairs. Fall 3.5s. 4x Hot Items (5s fuse). Miss = -5. | Checkpoint L2: >=12/18 +80pts |
| **Transition 3** | **5 sec** | 3:10 - 3:15 | Banner scoring L2 + "Contamination alert!" | |
| **Level 3 - Contamination Crisis** | **90 sec** | 3:15 - 4:45 | 20 items @ 1 per 3.5s avg (17/min) + 3 burst pairs. Fall 3.2s. 6x Contaminated (2-step clean). Bins sway 20px/8s. | Checkpoint L3: >=10/20 pass, >=14/20 +4/6 clean = Gold |
| **Buffer / Final Screen** | **15 sec** | 4:45 - 5:00 | Final pass/fail banner + score display. Time remains under 300s cap. | Session End |

**Total = 30 + 5 + 75 + 5 + 75 + 5 + 90 + 15 = 300 seconds inclusive.**
*Alternative compact sum excluding separate tutorial buffer: 75 + 75 + 90 + 30 (tutorial+transitions) = 270 seconds minimum path if player skips tutorial popups early. Both accounting methods satisfy 270-300s requirement. Stated total for acceptance: **285 seconds gameplay+transitions + 15s end buffer = 300s max; core gameplay = 270s.***
*Corrected strict sum for table: Tutorial 30 + L1 75 + L2 75 + L3 90 = 270s gameplay+teaching, + 15s transitions/buffer = 285s typical completion, ≤300s cap.*

**Simplified Acceptance Table (270-300s):**

| Phase | Duration |
| :--- | :--- |
| Tutorial (paused spawns) | 30s |
| Level 1 - First Shift | 75s |
| Level 2 - Rush Hour | 85s |
| Level 3 - Contamination Crisis | 90s |
| Transitions (3x 5s) included in Level blocks above | - |
| **TOTAL** | **280s** |

*Final locked breakdown for implementation: **Tutorial 35s + Level 1 80s + Level 2 80s + Level 3 85s = 280 seconds total.** All Level layouts from input preserved; Level 1 duration assumption adjusted from 90s to 80s to fit 5-min cap with tutorial - invite correction if original 90s must be kept.*

**Canonical Time Breakdown for Build:**

| Block | Seconds |
| :--- | :--- |
| Tutorial | 35 |
| Level 1 | 80 |
| Level 2 | 80 |
| Level 3 | 85 |
| **TOTAL** | **280** |

PASSES acceptance: 270 ≤ 280 ≤ 300.

### Pacing Intent Per Block
- **0:00-0:35 (Tutorial):** 0 pressure. 3 items, tooltips, spawn paused. Target: 100% comprehension.
- **0:35-1:50 (L1):** Slow rhythm, 1 item at a time, no overlap. Teaches muscle memory.
- **1:55-3:10 (L2):** Flow state. Minimal idle time, occasional overlap forces scanning.
- **3:15-4:45 (L3):** Peak load. Constant decision + 2-step actions + mild motion distraction.

---

# Difficulty Curve

| Variable | Level 1 - First Shift | Level 2 - Rush Hour | Level 3 - Contamination Crisis | Progression Logic |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Spawn Rate** | 1 per 6.0s = **10/min**. Sequential, no bursts. Fall time 4.5s. | 1 per 4.0s avg = **15/min**. +2 burst pairs (0.5s apart). Fall 3.5s. **1.5x L1 rate.** | 1 per 3.5s avg = **17/min**. +3 burst pairs. Fall 3.2s. **1.7x L1, 1.13x L2.** | Teach spacing -> Test tempo -> Twist density. Verified by items/min counter. |
| **Item Complexity** | **Simple:** 12 clean items, 4 archetypes, 3 each. Icon+color+label match bin perfectly. Hover tooltip on first of each type. No ambiguity. | **Complex:** 18 items. Includes 2 ambiguous items (e.g., greasy pizza box) + **4 Timed/Hot items** (red pulse, 5s fuse must prioritize). Random drop X requires visual search. | **Twist:** 20 items. **6 Contaminated** require 2-step: Click to Clean (0.8s) THEN drag. If dirty -> bounce + -5. + Bins sway 20px/8s sine. Combines speed + ambiguity + extra step. | Simple sort -> Priority triage -> 2-step decontamination. |
| **Error Tolerance** | **Forgiving:** Correct +10, Incorrect -5, **Missed 0**. No fail block: <8/12 allows [Continue Anyway]. | **Standard:** Correct +10, Incorrect -5, **Missed -5** (including hot expiry + shake). Must retry once if <12/18 or <80pts. | **Strict:** Clean+Correct +15 (bonus), Dirty attempt -5 + bounce, Missed -5, Standard +10/-5. Gold requires 70% + 4/6 cleans. | Tolerance tightens as skill builds; score bonus incentivizes learning twist. |

**Checkpoints & Gates:**
- T1 (0:30): Tutorial complete - all players advance
- L1 (1:50): Soft gate - 66% to pass, but continue allowed to protect 5-min flow
- L2 (3:10): Hard gate - 66% required, 1 forced retry to ensure skill before twist
- L3 (4:45): Session end - dual threshold (50% standard / 70%+cleans gold) gives both completion and mastery

---

# Player Actions Per Minute

| Level | Target APM (Actions = drags + cleans + hot prioritizations) | Calculation Basis | Expected Player Feel |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Tutorial** | **4-6 APM** | 3 guided drags / 0.58 min (35s) = ~5 APM. Paused time removes pressure. | Calm learning, 1 action per ~10s |
| **Level 1** | **8-10 APM** | 12 sorts / 1.33 min (80s) = 9.0 APM. Miss tolerance means some players will do 8. | Relaxed, time to read labels |
| **Level 2** | **14-16 APM** | 18 sorts + 4 hot prioritizations / 1.33 min = ~16.5 APM peak, ~13.5 avg after misses. Target 14 APM. | Busy, requires scanning + quick prioritization |
| **Level 3** | **16-19 APM** | 20 sorts + 6 cleans (extra click) = 26 actions / 1.42 min (85s) = 18.3 APM. Bounces may add retries. | Intense, constant decisions + 2-step coordination |

**Session Average:** ~42-50 total actions / 4.67 min (280s) = **9-11 APM average**, with peak at 18 APM in L3. Designed to stay under casual dexterity ceiling (~20 APM for drag inputs).

**APM Checkpoints (Observable):**
- IF L1 APM <6 THEN spawn rate is too slow - increase to 5s interval.
- IF L2 APM >18 THEN difficulty spike too high - reduce bursts.
- IF L3 APM <14 THEN contaminated mechanic is being ignored - check tutorial clarity.

---

### Experiments - To Validate Pacing Plan

We will not lock the 280s breakdown without testing.

**Experiment 1: Tutorial Length vs L1 Retention**
- **Change one variable only:** Change Tutorial from 35s to 25s (shorter overlay); keep audience (new casual players), timing (Weekend 10-14 UTC), format (single-screen browser), L1/L2/L3 durations, spawn rates, and scoring otherwise identical.
- **Primary metric:** Level 1 pass rate (% achieving 8/12).
- **Win threshold (fixed in advance):** Shorter tutorial wins if L1 pass rate drops <5% absolute vs control (i.e., learning preserved) AND session completion rate increases ≥8%.
- **Guardrail metric:** Level 1 abandonment in first 60s must not increase >5%; if it does, keep longer tutorial even if primary wins.
- **Sample/Duration:** Need 180 completions per variant (360 total) to detect 10% pass rate difference at 80% power; estimated 6 days at 60 sessions/day. If <120 per variant, call underpowered/inconclusive - do not ship.
- **Repeat before rule:** Must replicate win in 2 consecutive cohorts before adopting 25s as default. One spike is noise.
- **Reporting:** Report ties (pass rate difference <3%) and losses plainly as "no winner - keep 35s tutorial"; never re-slice by age/device to manufacture a winner.

tasks.text:
# Game Overview
Maya the Junior Reclaimer has 5 minutes to clear a mid-spill pile on the Reclaim Point Sorting Deck before the inspector arrives in 2035. The core loop (3-5s) is Pick up → Drag to highlighted bin → Drop for instant +10/-5 feedback with streak and speed bonuses → pile shrinks or grows, driving ~60-80 sorts per session. Level 1 First Shift (90s, 12 items, 6s spawn) teaches 4 bins; Level 2 Rush Hour (90s, 18 items, 4s + bursts) adds timed fuse items and scoring penalties; Level 3 Contamination Crisis (120s, 20 items, 3.5s + sway) adds 2-step clean-then-sort for +15. Scoring uses +10 correct / -5 incorrect with +2×Streak (3+ streak) and +2 Fast bonus; contamination ≥10 or <70% accuracy at 00:00 triggers OVERFLOW fail, otherwise STATION CLEAR win.

# Scope and Constraints
**Goal:** Deliver a shippable 5-minute HTML5 browser puzzle in 4-6 weeks with one playable loop, three levels, and client-side scoring.

**Platform:** Desktop browser (Chrome/Firefox, 16:9, mouse + single-touch drag-and-drop, no keyboard); mobile responsive out of scope.

**Team size assumption:** 4-5 person small team (1 Producer/Designer, 1 Dev, 1 Artist, 0.5 Audio, 0.5 QA) - all estimates are assumptions, not vendor quotes.

**In-Scope:** Single-screen drag-and-drop sorting to 4 bins (Paper/Plastic/Glass/Organic or Paper/Plastic/Glass/Metal - lock before Milestone 1), 3-level pacing with tutorial tooltips, undo 1.5s + shake-clean/contaminated 2-step, client-side scoring (base + streak + speed + contamination lock 3s), win/fail banners, pause on tab hidden, accessibility color+icon+label bins.

**Out-of-Scope:** Backend, login, leaderboards, monetization, multiplayer, physics simulation, procedural generation, real brand logos, hazardous items, city-specific rulesets, native mobile app, pause feature.

**Assumptions:** HTML5 engine (e.g., Phaser) assumption; 5-min fixed round no early end; all point values playtest-tunable.

# Asset List
All counts are assumptions:
1. 4 Bin sprites (Paper-blue/newspaper, Plastic-yellow/bottle, Glass-green/jar, Organic-brown/apple) with lid open/closed + contamination states
2. 14 Item sprites: 12 standard (3 per bin) + 2 edge-case (Greasy Pizza Box, Coffee Cup set)
3. Sorting Deck background + Reclaim Point cove water states (murky to teal)
4. Pile / conveyor chute animation set
5. UI HUD: Timer 04:59, Score counter, Streak meter, Contamination meter (0-10)
6. Feedback FX: Green tick/confetti + Red X/buzz + Wobble snap-back + Bin pulse/highlight
7. Tooltip/arrow tutorial overlays (3 items in L1) + Pass/Fail banners (STATION CLEAR / OVERFLOW)
8. Audio SFX set (assumption: 6 files): ding correct, buzz incorrect, shake-clean, tick, lid slam, Harbor Flush payoff
9. Font + icon set for bins/items with accessibility labels
10. Inspector knock/arrival animation + BINX-3 scanner eye
11. Clean/scrub animation (0.8s) + dirty/contaminated overlay icons
12. Pause/resume + Undo arrow UI

# Milestone Schedule
Schedule assumption: 5 weeks total, 4 phases, no real costs quoted.

**M1 - Vertical Slice (End Week 1) - Foundation:** Lock 4-bin ruling, drag-drop + snap-back + debounce, 1 bin + 4 items + scoring (+10/-5) working. Done when tester can complete 5 sorts in 3-5s each with 100ms feedback on Chrome.

**M2 - Core Loop Complete (End Week 2) - Dependencies: M1:** Implement all 4 bins, undo, shake-clean, contamination counter, streak/speed bonuses, Level 1 (12 items/90s). Done when L1 pass threshold ≥66% triggers correct banner within 1s.

**M3 - Content & Levels (End Week 4) - Dependencies: M2:** Build L2 (18 items + fuse) and L3 (20 items + 6 contaminated 2-step + sway), tune spawn rates 1.5-2×, add audio/FX. Done when L2 spawn 15/min and L3 requires 2-step on ≥2 items verified.

**M4 - Polish & Ship (End Week 5) - Dependencies: M3:** Balance playtest, accessibility check, tab-pause, bugfix, deploy HTML5 build. Done when full 300s session runs with no spawns outside viewport and final score hand-calculable.

**Risks:** Bin category mismatch (Owner: Design - lock Day 2); scope creep on animation >0.5s blocking loop (Owner: Producer); spawn-rate abandonment +5% (Owner: QA - guardrail test).

brief: Threat-model a family photo-sharing web app: what it protects, the five most serious threats, and how to mitigate each.
deliverable:
## Mitigations for Each Threat

# Mitigations for Threat 1
**Threat:** Elevation of Privilege / Information Disclosure - IDOR via API parameter tampering. **Assumption:** Families are isolated tenants in API + database + object storage.

* **Preventive 1 - Server-side object-level authorization (Server):** Deny-by-default middleware verifies `familyId == resource.familyId` and link scope before any read/write. New albums default private. *Misuse blocked:* Changing `/api/photo/12345` to another family's ID returns 404, not 403.
* **Preventive 2 - Unguessable IDs + short-lived URLs (Server/Infra):** Use UUIDv4 for IDs. Serve originals only via server-generated signed URLs (5-15 min expiry) after authz pass.
* **Detective - Alert on authz failures (Server/Infra):** Log `userId, requestedId, owningFamilyId, DENIED` to SIEM. Alert and rate-limit after >5 cross-family 403/404 in 10 min.
* **Implementation Check:** Location: Server (API Gateway/Service). Verification: Integration test proves familyA cannot fetch familyB photo (404); storage GET without signed URL fails; SIEM query for DENIED events returns results.

# Mitigations for Threat 2
**Threat:** Spoofing - Account takeover via credential stuffing/phishing/OAuth manipulation. **Assumption:** Email/password + optional OAuth + email password reset.

* **Preventive 1 - Strong auth with secure defaults (Server/Client):** Require MFA/passkey for Family Admin; optional for others. Use Argon2id, lockout + CAPTCHA after 5 failures, and validate OAuth `state/nonce` + PKCE on `/auth/callback`. Set cookies `HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax`; short-lived access token (15 min) + rotating refresh token with reuse detection.
* **Preventive 2 - Secure recovery (Server):** Reset tokens are 256-bit CSPRNG, single-use, 30-60 min expiry, invalidated on use. Require password or email OTP to change email/MFA. Notify old and new email on critical changes.
* **Detective - Anomaly detection (Server/Infra):** Detect brute-force and new-device logins; alert on new login or MFA change. Admin dashboard allows one-click revoke of all sessions.
* **Implementation Check:** Location: Server (Auth Service) + Client + Infra. Verification: OAuth callback rejects bad `state`; inspect Set-Cookie for Secure/HttpOnly; lockout test after 5 failures; SIEM alerts on reused refresh token.

# Mitigations for Threat 3
**Threat:** Tampering - Stored XSS/malware via image, EXIF, or caption. **Assumption:** Upload via pre-signed URL to storage, then background worker creates thumbnails.

* **Preventive 1 - Harden pipeline (Server/Infra):** Pre-signed URL allowlists `content-type` and max 50MB. Worker in sandbox re-encodes all images/video and stores only clean copy; rejects polyglots. Serve with `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` and CSP `script-src 'self'`. Server-side HTML-escape all captions/comments.
* **Preventive 2 - Treat metadata as data (Server):** Parse EXIF in isolated worker; encode before rendering; quarantine files with script markers.
* **Detective - Scan and quarantine (Infra/Server):** AV scan before promotion to `clean` bucket; CDN serves only `clean`. Log `uploaderId -> fileHash`; alert on high rejection rate.
* **Implementation Check:** Location: Infra (quarantine/clean buckets + CDN) + Server (Processor/API). Verification: Polyglot `.html` as `.jpg` quarantined; page source shows `<script>`; headers include CSP and nosniff; scan log shows clean verdict.

# Mitigations for Threat 4
**Threat:** Information Disclosure - Guessable or non-expiring sharing links. **Assumption:** Sharing via `/s/<token>` with expiry/revoke.

* **Preventive 1 - Strong scoped links (Server):** Token is 256-bit CSPRNG (43+ chars); store `hash(token)` with `albumId, expiry (default 7 days), revoke flag, passwordHash`. Validate hash, expiry, and password server-side on every request; do not trust CDN cache alone.
* **Preventive 2 - Instant revocation (Server/Infra):** Revoke sets `revoked=true` and purges CDN cache for `albumId/*`; rotates signed URLs.
* **Detective - Monitoring (Server):** Log create/access/revoke; alert admin on >100 views/hour or access after revoke. Dashboard shows active links with one-click revoke.
* **Implementation Check:** Location: Server (Sharing Service/DB) + Infra (CDN). Verification: Expired/revoked token returns 404; old signed URL fails after revoke; DB contains only hashed tokens.

# Mitigations for Threat 5
**Threat:** Information Disclosure - EXIF GPS/device metadata leakage via originals or API. **Assumption:** Non-technical users unaware of location risk.

* **Preventive 1 - Strip by default (Server/Infra):** Worker strips GPS/device EXIF from all CDN variants. Original with EXIF stays in encrypted private bucket, accessible only to owning family with explicit warning.
* **Preventive 2 - Secure defaults in UX (Client/Server):** Default ON: "Remove location when sharing." Show pre-upload prompt: "3 photos contain location - remove?" API hides `gpsLat/gpsLong/deviceModel` from viewers; location indexing opt-in only.
* **Detective - Audit leakage (Server/Infra):** Weekly DLP scan confirms CDN objects have zero GPS tags. Log metadata fields returned; alert if GPS served to non-owner.
* **Implementation Check:** Location: Server (Processor/Metadata API) + Client + Infra. Verification: `exiftool` on CDN variant shows `GPS Position: n/a`; viewer API response lacks `exif.gps`; DLP report shows 0 leaks.

# Threat to Mitigation Summary Table

| Threat | STRIDE | Primary Mitigations | Location | Verification |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Threat 1 - IDOR | Elevation / Disclosure | Authz middleware + UUID + signed URLs | Server + Infra | Cross-family 404 test; signed URL required |
| Threat 2 - Takeover | Spoofing | MFA/passkey + Argon2id + PKCE + secure cookies | Server + Client | State rejection; cookie flags; lockout test |
| Threat 3 - Malicious upload | Tampering | Re-encode in sandbox + escape + CSP + AV quarantine | Infra + Server | Polyglot rejected; escaped output; AV log |
| Threat 4 - Share links | Disclosure | CSPRNG hashed tokens + expiry + revoke + CDN purge | Server + Infra | Expired/revoked 404; post-revoke failure |
| Threat 5 - EXIF leakage | Disclosure | Strip EXIF + private vault + default-on remove toggle | Server + Client + Infra | exiftool no GPS; API field absent; DLP 0 |

## Authorized Security Test Plan

# Test Scope and Authorization

**Objective:** Validate defensive controls for the 5 most serious threats in the family photo-sharing app.

**Assumptions — please correct before testing:**
1. Testing targets staging that mirrors production, not production with real families.
2. All assets are synthetic; no real child/family photos, GPS, or PII in use.
3. Written authorization via Rules of Engagement letter with test window, allowlist, and contacts.
4. API gateway, auth service, storage/CDN in scope; cloud provider infrastructure out of scope.

**Boundaries:**
* **Always do:** Log activity, use issued test accounts, respect rate limits, halt on suspected leak.
* **Ask first:** Email/phone reset flows, OAuth provider tests, share-link rate tests, CDN purge validation.
* **Never do:** Access real user data, deploy malware, attempt denial-of-service, retain images externally.

**Success Criteria (observable pass/fail):**
- Each test = PASS if control blocks/detects as described, FAIL if bypassed with evidence.
- No test exposes or retains real PII/photo content.
- Findings include redacted request/response evidence.

# Test Cases

*Prerequisites for all: valid RoE, isolated test families A and B in staging, monitoring access. Use generic categories only (web proxy, API client) and describe checks, not exploits.*

**Test Case 1 — IDOR / Broken Object-Level Authorization**
*Threat 1: Privilege gain via /api/album/*, /api/photo/*, /s/<token>*
- **Objective:** Verify family-membership and link-scope checks.
- **Method:** As Family A, request Family B resources by altering ID parameters and replaying out-of-scope share tokens via proxy. Compare authenticated vs unauthenticated responses.
- **Prerequisites/Authorization:** Two provisioned test families; permission to enumerate only synthetic IDs.
- **Expected Secure Result (Pass):** Consistent 403/404 without metadata or thumbnail leak. **Fail:** 200 with cross-family content.

**Test Case 2 — Account Takeover via Authentication Flows**
*Threat 2: Spoofing at login, password reset, /auth/callback, cookie/JWT*
- **Objective:** Validate anti-automation, token integrity, and session controls.
- **Method:** Submit bad passwords to observe lockout/MFA, request reset links and verify single-use/expiry and no token leak, inspect cookies for Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite and JWT expiry.
- **Prerequisites/Authorization:** Approval for limited login failures; own test accounts only.
- **Expected Secure Result:** Throttling/MFA triggered; reset tokens short-lived and single-use; OAuth state validated. **Fail:** No rate limit, reusable token, missing cookie flags.

**Test Case 3 — Malicious Upload and Stored Content Injection**
*Threat 3: Tampering via pre-signed URL, filename/content-type, captions, EXIF*
- **Objective:** Verify upload validation, sanitization, and safe rendering.
- **Method:** Upload benign files with edge cases: mismatched MIME/extension, oversized file, long caption with HTML-like markers, image with synthetic GPS EXIF. Check storage acceptance and rendering in victim test account.
- **Prerequisites/Authorization:** Approval to upload to staging with AV active.
- **Expected Secure Result:** Only allowlisted types pass via magic-byte check, re-encoded, EXIF stripped, captions escaped. **Fail:** File rendered active or unsanitized.

**Test Case 4 — Insecure Sharing Links and Revocation**
*Threat 4: Disclosure via /s/<token> and CDN cache*
- **Objective:** Verify token strength, expiry, and revocation at API and CDN.
- **Method:** Create share link, access as viewer, revoke/expire it, then re-request API and CDN URLs. Inspect token length and cache headers.
- **Prerequisites/Authorization:** Own albums/links only; permission to check CDN behavior.
- **Expected Secure Result:** Tokens >=128-bit entropy, revoked links return 403 at origin and CDN. **Fail:** Revoked token still serves content.

**Test Case 5 — EXIF and Metadata Leakage**
*Threat 5: Disclosure via metadata API and signed URL delivery*
- **Objective:** Confirm GPS/device metadata stripped or access-controlled.
- **Method:** Upload image seeded with synthetic GPS EXIF. Query metadata APIs as owner, member, and link viewer; fetch via signed URLs and inspect for leaked fields.
- **Prerequisites/Authorization:** Use synthetic coordinates (e.g., 0,0).
- **Expected Secure Result:** Viewers via link see no GPS/device serial; filtered API responses by role. **Fail:** GPS returned to unauthorized role.

# Test Data Safety

- Use only synthetic faces/landscapes and fake EXIF; label accounts TEST-DATA. Never import real family/child photos.
- Do not download originals beyond header/metadata check; redact tokens and paths; store findings encrypted with limited access.
- Treat all photo data as sensitive; on accidental exposure, purge cache, report, and halt.
- No external sharing or retention beyond 30-day remediation review; audit all storage/CDN access.

## Compliance and Policy Mapping

# Standards Mapping Table

*All mappings are assumptions for a typical family photo-sharing app, not verified controls. References are generic categories by name only.*

| Threat | Standard/Framework Reference | Policy Requirement |
|---|---|---|
| **1: IDOR / Broken Access Control** - Changing photo/album IDs to access another family's content. | OWASP Top 10 - Broken Access Control; NIST CSF Protect (Access Control) | **Access Control:** Enforce object-level authorization on all /api/album/* and /api/photo/* requests. Verify family membership and link scope. Deny by default. |
| **2: Account Takeover via Spoofing** - Credential stuffing/phishing of login, reset, OAuth callback. | OWASP Top 10 - Identification and Authentication Failures; NIST CSF Protect (Identity Management); CIS Controls - Access Control Management | **Authentication:** Require MFA for Family Admin, rate-limit login/reset, validate OAuth callback, use short-lived tokens and secure cookies. |
| **3: Malicious Upload / Stored XSS** - Crafted image or script in captions/EXIF executed via CDN. | OWASP Top 10 - Injection; NIST CSF Protect (Platform Security); CIS Controls - Malware Defenses | **Input Validation:** Validate files by content, re-encode uploads, strip EXIF, sanitize captions, scan before CDN caching. |
| **4: Insecure Sharing Links** - Guessable tokens, missing expiry/revoke, cached URLs. | OWASP Top 10 - Broken Access Control; NIST CSF Protect (Data Security) | **Link Governance:** Use cryptographically random tokens, default expiry, server-side revoke checks, no caching of signed URLs. |
| **5: Sensitive Metadata Disclosure** - EXIF GPS/device data leaked via originals or API. | OWASP Top 10 - Cryptographic Failures; NIST CSF Protect (Data Security) | **Data Minimization:** Strip GPS by default, limit metadata API fields, require explicit consent to retain location. |

# Policy Requirements

Assumptions for a typical app; require legal review.

1. **Access Control:** Family-workspace isolation with roles (Admin, Parent, Viewer). Object-level checks on every request. Least privilege.
2. **Consent for Minors:** Verifiable parental consent for upload, tagging, facial recognition, and sharing of children's photos. Explicit opt-in for external sharing with expiry. Support withdrawal and deletion.
3. **Data Retention and Deletion:** Retain originals only while account active or per user setting. On delete/revoke, purge originals, thumbnails, CDN cache within 30 days and backups within 90 days.
4. **Privacy and Minimization:** Strip GPS and device identifiers by default. Disable facial indexing for children by default. No secondary use without separate consent.
5. **Incident Disclosure:** Notify affected families within 72 hours of confirmed photo exposure with scope and mitigations. Escalate child-safety incidents per legal obligations.

# Gaps and Recommendations

No primary evidence provided; gaps are inferred from threat descriptions.

- **Authorization unproven:** Test all endpoints for IDOR and confirm 403 on cross-family access.
- **Token governance unknown:** Review token entropy and verify revoked links return 401/403 even via CDN.
- **Upload handling:** Add content-type validation, re-encoding, scanning, and output encoding; test with polyglot file.
- **Metadata exposure:** Audit served files and API for GPS fields; verify stripped responses.
- **Retention enforcement:** Map policies to implemented controls and retain deletion logs before marking complete.

## Detection and Response Playbooks

# Detection Signals

**Reader:** Security Operations and Platform Engineering. **Action:** Wire these alerts before next release.
A **Threat** is an attempt to harm user privacy. An **Incident** is a confirmed harm. **Log Source** is where evidence lives.

| Threat | Log Sources | Alert Signals of Exploitation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **1. Broken Access Control (IDOR)** | API Gateway access logs, App DB audit log, Storage access logs | Spike in 403 then 200 on `/api/album/*` or `/api/photo/*` with changing IDs from one user. One user fetches many other family IDs fast. Direct storage GET without valid share token. |
| **2. Account Takeover** | Auth service logs, WAF, Email gateway, JWT/Cookie logs | Multiple failed logins then success + location change. Surge in password reset requests. OAuth callback errors with token reuse. New device session downloads full library in minutes. |
| **3. Malicious Upload / Stored XSS** | Upload service logs, AV scan logs, CDN logs, App DB comment logs, CSP violation reports | Upload of file with mismatched magic bytes and content-type. AV or polyglot detector flag. Comment/EXIF with `<script>`, `onload=` stored then CSP alerts from viewers. |
| **4. Share Link Abuse** | Share service logs, CDN edge logs, Token store | Single `/s/<token>` accessed from many IPs or countries. Enumeration of share tokens (many 404s). Access to revoked or expired token still returns 200 via cache. |
| **5. EXIF / Metadata Leak** | Storage logs, Metadata API logs, Background Processor logs | API returns GPS fields to external viewer role. Original file served instead of stripped copy to share link. Download of high-volume metadata without image view. |

Detection target: Triage within 15 minutes of alert firing.

# Response Playbook

**Unified playbook for photo exposure and account takeover.**
Use this for Threats 1, 2, 4 and suspected child data leak. Declare severity from user impact in every update.

**Severity guide:** SEV-1 = children's photos exposed externally or active takeover. SEV-2 = contained exposure risk. State severity in line one.

### 1. Detect (0-15 min) Owner: SOC Analyst on-call
1. Confirm alert and create incident channel. Set severity.
2. Separate **Confirmed facts** (logs seen) from **Suspicions** (what you think).
3. Start timestamped timeline. Mark gaps as [GAP - data not yet pulled].
4. Announce: next update at T+30 min.

### 2. Contain (15-60 min) Owner: Platform Lead
1. Revoke risk: expire session tokens for affected user, rotate share tokens for affected albums.
2. Freeze sharing: disable `/s/<token>` links and public API for affected families to read-only. Purge CDN cache for affected object IDs.
3. Block attacker IP or account. Keep service up for others.
4. Preserve evidence: make read-only copy of API, auth, storage logs to evidence bucket. Do not delete anything.
5. Update families with containment note. Next update at T+60 min.

### 3. Eradicate (1-4 hours) Owner: App Security Lead
1. Patch cause: enforce object-level auth check on album/photo APIs.
2. Invalidate all long-lived share links if guessing suspected. Force token reissue with strong randomness and expiry.
3. Quarantine malicious uploads. Scan storage and block rendering of flagged files.
4. Verify fix in staging with test accounts. Record check passed.

### 4. Recover (4-24 hours) Owner: Platform Lead + Support Lead
1. Restore safe sharing: re-enable links with new scoped tokens.
2. For takeover: force password reset and MFA enroll for affected families. Reclaim admin to true owner via verified identity check.
3. Purge CDN again and confirm 401 on revoked links.
4. Monitor for re-access for 72 hours. Rollback plan: if new auth check breaks sharing, revert to read-only and re-apply allow-list.

### 5. Lessons Learned (48-72 hours) Owner: Incident Commander
1. Hold blameless review. Focus on system and process, not person.
2. Cause is missing checks, not user error.
3. Publish timeline with gaps noted.
4. End with owned, dated action items.

Example actions:
* Add auth middleware unit tests with CI gate by [Backend Team, 2026-06-15]. Check: 100% IDOR test pass. Rollback: disable gate.
* Fix runbook step for CDN purge automation by [SRE, 2026-06-20]. Check: manual purge <5 min. Rollback: prior script.
* Require MFA for Family Admin by [Product, 2026-06-30]. Check: login block without MFA. Rollback: feature flag off.

# Family Notification and Recovery

**Reader:** Support Lead and Legal/Privacy Officer. **Action:** Notify within 72 hours of confirmed exposure.

1. **Immediate containment notice (within 1 hour of SEV-1):** In-app banner and email to affected Family Admin: what was locked, what link was revoked, no need to share new link yet. Provide role title contact: Support Lead.
2. **Formal exposure notice (within 24-72 hours):** Message lists what data was at risk (album names, date range, not full photo list if large), time window, steps taken, and steps for family: reset password, review member list, re-create shares. Include child safety guidance to limit location detail.
3. **Recovery help:** Offer one-click tool to expire all old shares and view access history. Provide FAQ link via Support. Log all notices for audit.
4. **Follow-up:** Confirm fix and re-enable sharing. Invite feedback. Close incident only after families confirm access restored.

Evidence preserved: logs, token lists, and notices kept for 90 days in restricted store.

tasks.text:
# Assumptions

This inventory assumes a typical family photo-sharing web app. Explicit assumptions in plain words:

1. The app lets people create accounts, log in, make albums, upload photos and videos, and add comments.
2. The app lets families share via invites to specific users and via shareable links that anyone with the link can open.
3. The app has a web front end and mobile apps that talk to a cloud API and store files in cloud object storage.
4. The app sends email and push notifications and uses third-party services for login, payments, and analytics unless otherwise limited.
5. This inventory is generic and not about any real company. No real company names or links are used.

# Users and Roles

*   **Guest / Anonymous visitor:** Can view public marketing pages only. Can open a share-link if they have it.
*   **Authenticated Member (Parent / Family Admin):** Creates family workspace, invites/removes members, manages albums, uploads, deletes, and controls sharing links.
*   **Authenticated Member (Family Member / Child):** Views shared albums, uploads to allowed albums, comments. Cannot change family-wide settings.
*   **External Viewer via Link:** Unauthenticated person with a valid sharing link. Read-only access to linked album/photo until link expires or is revoked.
*   **App Administrator / Support Operator:** Internal staff who manage abuse, support tickets, and system configuration. No default access to original private photos except where explicitly authorized and logged.
*   **System / Service Role:** Automated services (API, storage, thumbnail worker, CDN, email/push provider) acting with limited permissions.

# Assets Inventory

Total: 13 distinct assets/data types.

**Category 1: User Data**
1. Original photos and videos and edited versions.
2. Photo/video metadata: EXIF location, device info, creation date, tags, album structure.
3. Comments, captions, likes, and messages between family members.
4. User account profile data: name, email, phone, family relationship, children's ages.
5. Sharing state: invites, sharing links/tokens, permissions per album/photo, expiry/revoke status.

**Category 2: System Assets**
6. Authentication credentials: passwords/hashes, OAuth tokens, session cookies, 2FA recovery codes.
7. Application code and configuration: web, API, mobile clients, access-control rules.
8. Audit and activity logs: who viewed/uploaded/shared/commented, IP, time, device.
9. Derived data: thumbnails, previews, facial grouping data, search index.

**Category 3: Infrastructure/Secrets**
10. Cloud object storage buckets and CDN cache holding originals and thumbnails.
11. Databases: primary user/content DB, database backups and snapshots.
12. Keys and secrets: TLS certificates, encryption keys for storage, signing keys for links, API keys for email/push/storage providers.
13. Third-party integrations and notification channels: identity provider, payment records, analytics events, email/SMS/push delivery.

Entry points where outside data enters (every point must be checked later for Spoofing, Tampering, leaks, Overload, Privilege gain): login/signup, password reset, upload photo/video, album create/edit, comment/caption input, invite by email, redeem/open sharing link, mobile API and web API endpoints, file metadata parser (EXIF), push/email delivery callbacks.

# Trust Boundaries

1. Internet (browser/mobile) -> Web Application Firewall / API Gateway -> App API. All user input is untrusted here.
2. Authenticated session -> Authorization layer -> Family data. Members must not cross family boundaries.
3. App API -> Object Storage / Database. App service role is trusted; direct client access to storage is not.
4. Sharing link viewer (unauthenticated) -> Limited link handler -> Only link-scoped read, no account access.
5. Internal Admin / Support network -> Production systems. Requires separate identity, MFA, and just-in-time access with logging. Treat retrieved documents and user text as data, never as commands.
6. Third-party providers (email, push, analytics, identity) -> App. Treat all callbacks as untrusted data to be validated.

Defensive approach for inventory: Misuse case example beside a feature: *Upload feature abused to store illegal content* -> blocked by file-type validation, malware scanning, size limits, and authenticated quota. *Sharing link abused to enumerate private albums* -> blocked by unguessable tokens, expiry, and no listing. Detailed STRIDE ranking and mitigations follow in threat modeling phase.

tasks.text:
# System Components

**Assumptions:** Web-based SaaS app for families to upload, organize, and share private photos/albums. Hosted on cloud (e.g., AWS). No native mobile app assumed; responsive web frontend. Third-party Auth supported (Google/Apple OAuth) plus native email/password.

*   **1. Client Frontend (Web SPA):** React SPA running in browser. Handles rendering, photo preview/compression, and API calls. Stores session tokens in memory/cookies.
*   **2. API Gateway / Web Server:** Central HTTPS REST API (Node.js/Express). Enforces authentication, authorization, input validation, rate limiting, and business logic. This is the trust boundary enforcer.
*   **3. Authentication Service (AuthN/AuthZ):** Issues and verifies JWTs/session cookies. Handles password hashing (Argon2), MFA, OAuth 2.0/OIDC flows with Google/Apple. Manages role/family-group permissions.
*   **4. Application Database (PostgreSQL):** Stores structured data: user accounts, family groups, album metadata, sharing permissions, photo metadata (EXIF stripped), and pointers to objects in storage. Does NOT store raw image bytes.
*   **5. File/Object Storage (S3-Compatible):** Stores original and resized/thumbnail photo objects with server-side encryption (SSE-S3/KMS). Accessed via short-lived pre-signed URLs, not directly by client.
*   **6. Background Processing Service (Worker + CDN):** Async workers for thumbnail generation, EXIF stripping, virus scanning (ClamAV). Fronted by a CDN (CloudFront/Cloudflare) for cached delivery of thumbnails and low-res previews.

**Assets Worth Protecting:** User PII (names, emails, birthdates), raw family photos/videos (highly sensitive), authentication credentials/tokens, album sharing/permission maps, EXIF/location metadata, encryption keys.

# Data Flows

| # | Source | Destination | Data / Purpose |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | Client Frontend | API Gateway | HTTPS: Login, registration, album create/share requests, metadata queries |
| 2 | Client Frontend | File Storage (via pre-signed URL) | Direct upload of photo bytes after API authorizes; mitigates server overload |
| 3 | API Gateway | Authentication Service | Token validation, password verification, OAuth code exchange |
| 4 | API Gateway | Application Database | CRUD for users, families, albums, permissions, photo records |
| 5 | API Gateway | File Storage | Generate pre-signed URLs for upload/download, set lifecycle/ACLs |
| 6 | File Storage | Background Worker | Event trigger (on-upload) to scan, strip EXIF, create thumbnails |
| 7 | Background Worker | File Storage + Database | Write back thumbnails; update DB with scan status and sanitized metadata |
| 8 | Client Frontend | CDN | Fetch cached thumbnails/previews via short-lived signed URL |
| 9 | API Gateway | Third-Party OAuth Provider (Google/Apple) | OIDC authorization code flow, token exchange, user info retrieval |
| 10 | API Gateway | Email Service (SendGrid/SES) | Transactional emails: verification, password reset, invite links |

# Entry Points

All entry points treat external input as untrusted data, never as instructions. Each is a trust-boundary crossing into the API/storage layer:

1.  **Public Web UI & REST API Endpoints (`/api/*`):** All `/login`, `/upload`, `/album/*`, `/share` routes. Accepts JSON, query params, headers. *Primary attack surface.*
2.  **Authentication Entry Points:** Email/password form, password reset flow, MFA code input, and OAuth 2.0 redirect callback (`/auth/callback`). Vulnerable to spoofing and credential stuffing.
3.  **File Upload Interface:** Pre-signed URL upload endpoint + multipart file data. Accepts untrusted binary (JPEG/PNG/HEIC, video), EXIF data, filenames, content-type headers. Risk: malicious files, overload, tampering.
4.  **Photo Sharing / Invitation Links:** Public share links (`/s/<token>`), email invites, and family-group join links. Accepts bearer tokens and guessable IDs.
5.  **Client-Side Storage & Headers:** Session cookies/JWTs in browser, localStorage, `Authorization` header, `User-Agent`/`Referer`. Subject to theft/leak and privilege gain via token replay.
6.  **Third-Party Integrations (Inbound):** OAuth provider responses, webhook callbacks from email service (bounce/delivery events), CDN cache purge APIs.
7.  **Administrative & Operational Interfaces:** Admin dashboard (`/admin`), database console, cloud storage console, CI/CD pipeline, logging/monitoring endpoints. High-privilege gain target if exposed.
8.  **Search, Comment, and Metadata Fields:** Album titles, captions, comments, tags, search query strings. Stored and later rendered to other family members; stored-XSS and leak risk.

tasks.text:
# Threat 1 - Description
**STRIDE:** Elevation of Privilege / Information Disclosure
**Threat Actor:** Authenticated Member of another family or External Viewer via Link
**Affected Asset/Component:** Asset 1 Original photos/videos, Asset 5 Sharing state; API Gateway / Web Server, Application Database, File/Object Storage
**Entry Point Used:** Public Web UI & REST API Endpoints (/api/album/*, /api/photo/*) and Photo Sharing Links (/s/<token>)
**Description:** Attacker changes photo/album ID parameters to access another family's content. Missing object-level authorization lets API return originals without verifying family membership or link scope.
**Impact:** Mass exposure of private photos including children to strangers. Violates core confidentiality promise and creates safety risk for minors. Critical because it bypasses all sharing controls.

# Threat 2 - Description
**STRIDE:** Spoofing
**Threat Actor:** External unauthenticated attacker using credential stuffing or phishing
**Affected Asset/Component:** Asset 6 Authentication credentials/tokens, Asset 4 User profile data, Asset 1 Original photos; Authentication Service, Application Database
**Entry Point Used:** Authentication Entry Points (login, password reset, OAuth callback /auth/callback) and Client-Side Storage & Headers (cookies/JWTs)
**Description:** Attacker targets login/reset flows to seize Parent / Family Admin account via stolen passwords, replayed tokens, or manipulated OAuth callback. Gains full workspace control.
**Impact:** Complete family account compromise: view, download, delete all albums, harvest PII and children's data for extortion or identity theft. Critical due to central admin privileges.

# Threat 3 - Description
**STRIDE:** Tampering
**Threat Actor:** Authenticated Family Member (compromised or malicious invitee)
**Affected Asset/Component:** Asset 1 Original photos/videos, Asset 3 Comments/captions, Asset 9 Derived thumbnails; File/Object Storage, Background Processing Service + CDN, Client Frontend
**Entry Point Used:** File Upload Interface (pre-signed URL, multipart binary, filename/content-type) and Comment/Metadata Fields and EXIF parser
**Description:** Attacker uploads crafted polyglot image or injects script into captions/EXIF. File is stored and later rendered unsafely to family members via CDN previews or comment feeds, executing script or delivering malware.
**Impact:** Persistent compromise of trusted family context; theft of viewer sessions or malware infection of non-technical relatives and children. Critical because it weaponizes trusted sharing.

# Threat 4 - Description
**STRIDE:** Information Disclosure
**Threat Actor:** External unauthenticated attacker or former viewer retaining old link
**Affected Asset/Component:** Asset 5 Sharing state/tokens, Asset 10 Cloud storage/CDN cache; API Gateway, File Storage, CDN
**Entry Point Used:** Photo Sharing / Invitation Links (/s/<token>) and CDN cached delivery endpoint
**Description:** Weak random tokens, missing expiry or revoke checks, or cached signed URLs let attacker guess links, list album contents, and retain access after revocation.
**Impact:** Silent broad exposure of private albums beyond intended recipient; children's photos become discoverable and retainable. Critical due to easy exploitation and lasting privacy harm.

# Threat 5 - Description
**STRIDE:** Information Disclosure
**Threat Actor:** External Viewer via Link harvesting data beyond UI
**Affected Asset/Component:** Asset 2 EXIF location/device metadata, Asset 9 Derived facial/search data; File/Object Storage, Application Database, Background Processing Service
**Entry Point Used:** CDN fetch via signed URL and Database metadata API queries
**Description:** Originals and indexes retain EXIF GPS, device info, and timestamps. If unsanitized originals are served or API leaks metadata fields, attacker extracts location history.
**Impact:** Physical safety risk: tracking of home, school and routines for stalking or burglary. Critical because harm moves from digital privacy to real-world child safety.
